brief.meaningEn: Regard someone or something as less worthy or inferior.
brief.meaningZh: 認為某人或某事較低等、不值得尊重。
brief.grammar: look down on + person/activity; inseparable, not look someone down on.
brief.register: Common disapproving phrasal verb.
brief.boundaryZh: 本課是輕視態度，不是站高處往下看；客觀指出不足或不同意，不一定代表看不起。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可以要求改進而尊重對方；也不能只憑對方經驗較少就貶低其價值。
brief.outcomeZh: 能分辨尊重的回饋與把人看低的態度。

listening.en: The coach did not look down on beginners; she treated their questions seriously and helped them practise the basics.
listening.zh: 教練沒有看不起初學者；她認真對待問題，並幫他們練基本功。

options.en: She treated less experienced learners with respect.
options.zh: 她尊重經驗較少的學員。

options.en: She regarded their questions as beneath her attention.
options.zh: 她認為他們的問題不值得理會。

options.en: She accepted only learners who had already mastered the basics.
options.zh: 她只接受已掌握基本功的學員。

options.en: She avoided giving feedback because beginners could not improve.
options.zh: 她因認為初學者無法進步而避免回饋。

listening.explanationZh: 認真對待及幫助顯示尊重；not look down on 否定輕視，不是免去指導。

reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼覺得教練尊重初學者？
reply.promptEn: Why do you think the coach respected the beginners?

options.en: She took their questions seriously.
options.zh: 她認真對待他們的問題。

options.en: She did not look down on them for lacking experience.
options.zh: 她沒有因他們缺乏經驗而看不起他們。

options.en: She gave them patient help with the basics.
options.zh: 她耐心幫他們練基本功。

options.en: She treated them as learners worth supporting.
options.zh: 她視他們為值得支持的學習者。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都提出尊重的證據；金句直接否定輕視態度。

scene.promptZh: 新組員不熟悉軟件，資深組員說「連這個都不懂，不值得加入我們」，也不聽解釋。哪句貼切？

options.en: The experienced member gave specific, respectful advice about the next step.
options.zh: 資深組員就下一步給具體而尊重的建議。

options.en: The experienced member looked down on the newcomer for lacking a skill.
options.zh: 資深組員因新手欠缺一項技能而看不起他。

options.en: The experienced member recognised the newcomer’s value while discussing training needs.
options.zh: 資深組員討論訓練需要時肯定新手價值。

scene.explanationZh: 不值得加入的貶低把技能不足推及人的價值，與尊重回饋不同。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不宜只憑這點就說 look down on someone？

options.en: A tutor identifies an error, explains it kindly and offers practice.
options.zh: 導師指出錯誤、友善解釋並提供練習。

options.en: A member says a novice is not worth listening to because of their background.
options.zh: 組員因新手背景而說其意見不值得聽。

options.en: A judge dismisses an entrant as inferior without considering the work.
options.zh: 評審未看作品就把參賽者視作低人一等。

contrast.explanationZh: 指出錯誤可以是尊重的協助；輕視需有把人看低的態度證據。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說老師要求他重寫一段，就一定是 look down on him。哪句澄清較準確？

options.en: The revision request alone does not show contempt; how did the teacher explain it?
options.zh: 單憑重寫要求未能顯示輕視；老師怎樣解釋？

options.en: Rewrite only to stop further comments, without asking what needs improvement.
options.zh: 只為停止更多評論而重寫，不用問哪裏需改善。

options.en: The extra work alone proves disrespect, regardless of the teacher’s explanation.
options.zh: 不論老師解釋甚麼，單憑多了工作就證明不尊重。

dialogue.explanationZh: 需聽老師解釋及查看回饋內容，不只為避評而改，也不只憑多了工作就斷定輕視。

speaking.en: We should not look down on people who are still learning the basics.
speaking.zh: 我們不應看不起仍在學基本功的人。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再表達對學習者的尊重。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：朋友因一位街坊做清潔工作，就認為不值得聽他的社區意見。你想提醒尊重不同工作，應按意見內容評估。用一至兩句英文回應。

examples.en: We should not look down on him because of his job. His views on the neighbourhood deserve a fair hearing.
examples.zh: 我們不應因他的工作而看不起他。他對社區的看法值得公平聽取。

examples.en: Looking down on a cleaner ignores the value of the work; let us consider what he says about the neighbourhood.
examples.zh: 看不起清潔工忽略了工作的價值；一起考慮他對社區說的內容吧。

writing.selfCheckZh: 反對以職業把人看低，仍按意見內容作判斷，不假定職業決定意見品質。

takeaways.en: She never looked down on colleagues with less experience.
takeaways.zh: 她從不看不起經驗較少的同事。

takeaways.en: Giving honest advice does not mean looking down on someone.
takeaways.zh: 給真誠建議不代表看不起某人。

brief.meaningEn: Hinder an activity, relationship or progress by creating an obstacle or interference.
brief.meaningZh: 造成障礙或干擾，妨礙活動、關係或進展。
brief.grammar: get in the way of + noun/-ing; may describe noise, interruptions, pride or objects.
brief.register: Common conventional spatial expression, literal or figurative according to context.
brief.boundaryZh: 本課聚焦干擾，不必完全阻止；與275生活事務打亂計劃的特定說法相關，但可用多種具體主語及障礙。
brief.misconceptionZh: 有妨礙不表示能力差或永遠做不到；需辨認哪個干擾影響甚麼活動。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指明障礙與受影響活動，提出針對性的調整。

listening.en: Constant message alerts got in the way of my reading, so I put the phone aside while I finished the chapter.
listening.zh: 不斷的訊息提示妨礙我閱讀，所以讀完那章期間我把手機放到一旁。

options.en: The reader had finished the chapter before any alerts arrived.
options.zh: 任何提示出現前，讀者已完成該章。

options.en: Repeated alerts interrupted the reader’s attention.
options.zh: 重複提示打斷讀者注意力。

options.en: The alerts supplied notes that improved the reader’s understanding.
options.zh: 提示提供筆記，改善讀者理解。

options.en: The reader chose a new chapter because the original subject was unfamiliar.
options.zh: 讀者因原本主題陌生而選了新章節。

listening.explanationZh: constant alerts 是干擾，put the phone aside 是針對來源的調整；沒有說不懂主題。

reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼閱讀時把手機放到一旁？
reply.promptEn: Why did you put your phone aside while reading?

options.en: The alerts kept interrupting my attention.
options.zh: 提示不斷打斷我的注意力。

options.en: I wanted fewer message interruptions while finishing the chapter.
options.zh: 我想讀完該章時少些訊息干擾。

options.en: The alerts were getting in the way of my reading.
options.zh: 提示正妨礙我閱讀。

options.en: The repeated notifications made it harder to stay with the text.
options.zh: 重複通知讓我更難專心看文章。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都解釋干擾及調整原因；金句指明受影響的閱讀活動。

scene.promptZh: 兩位組員有想法，但彼此怕承認誤會，遲遲無法坦白合作。哪句描述態度造成的障礙？

options.en: Their pride is helping them clarify the misunderstanding.
options.zh: 他們的自尊正幫他們釐清誤會。

options.en: Their pride is getting in the way of an honest conversation.
options.zh: 他們的自尊正妨礙坦誠對話。

options.en: They have already discussed the misunderstanding openly and resolved it.
options.zh: 他們已公開討論並解決誤會。

scene.explanationZh: 怕承認誤會令溝通難以開始，是態度干擾，不是已解決。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不符合 get in the way of careful work？

options.en: Frequent unrelated interruptions break concentration.
options.zh: 頻繁的無關打斷破壞專注。

options.en: An unresolved disagreement prevents members from sharing necessary information.
options.zh: 未解決分歧妨礙成員分享必要資訊。

options.en: A planned quiet period lets the group complete a careful check.
options.zh: 預留的安靜時段讓小組完成仔細查核。

contrast.explanationZh: 安靜時段有助仔細工作；其餘都提供具體阻礙。

dialogue.promptZh: 同學說「噪音 got in the way，所以我一定永遠讀不懂這篇」。哪句回應最準確？

options.en: The noise disrupted this attempt; trying in a quieter place may help.
options.zh: 噪音干擾了這次嘗試；換安靜地方可能有幫助。

options.en: The interruption shows the text is too advanced, so we should replace it with an easier one.
options.zh: 打斷顯示文章太深，所以應換較簡單文章。

options.en: This interrupted session is enough to conclude that a quieter setting would not help.
options.zh: 單憑這次受干擾閱讀，已足以斷定安靜環境不會有幫助。

dialogue.explanationZh: 已知噪音干擾這次嘗試；先試較安靜環境，不憑中斷就斷定文章太深或永遠讀不懂。

speaking.en: Repeated interruptions get in the way of careful work.
speaking.zh: 反覆打斷會妨礙仔細工作。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出甚麼干擾哪項活動。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：排練室入口堆着你們的行李，其他組員要進出便需繞路。你想把行李移到議定存放處，讓入口暢通。用一至兩句英文說明阻礙與調整。

examples.en: Our luggage is getting in the way of people using the entrance, so we should move it to the agreed storage area.
examples.zh: 我們的行李正妨礙人使用入口，所以應把它移到議定存放處。

examples.en: The bags get in the way when the group enters the room. Let us clear the entrance and use the storage space instead.
examples.zh: 小組進房時，袋子造成阻礙。清空入口，改用存放空間吧。

writing.selfCheckZh: 把具體物件與進出受阻連起來，再提出移往議定位置；不只描述行李存在。

takeaways.en: Noise can get in the way of a thoughtful conversation.
takeaways.zh: 噪音可以妨礙深入對話。

takeaways.en: Do not let a minor disagreement get in the way of sharing useful information.
takeaways.zh: 不要讓小分歧妨礙分享有用資訊。

brief.meaningEn: Close enough for someone to reach with an arm without moving far.
brief.meaningZh: 近得讓人伸手便可碰到或取用，不必走遠。
brief.grammar: keep/place something within arm’s reach; a conventional proximity phrase.
brief.register: Common expression; taught literally for accessible objects in this lesson.
brief.boundaryZh: 表示很近而可伸手取，不表示已拿在手、免費、較重要或一定最適合；需考慮實際擺放。
brief.misconceptionZh: 同一房間不一定夠近；可看見也不等於伸手可及。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述物件方便取用的位置，區分可見、附近與伸手可及。

sources.sentence: I keep my notes within arm's reach during class.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 2, table 2, row 2; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: I kept the reference card within arm’s reach beside my notebook, so I could check it without leaving the desk.
listening.zh: 我把參考卡放在筆記本旁、伸手可及的位置，讓我不離開書桌就能查看。

options.en: It was already held in the speaker’s hand throughout the task.
options.zh: 說話者全程已把它拿在手中。

options.en: It was visible on a shelf across the room but too far to touch.
options.zh: 它在房間另一端架上看得見，但遠得碰不到。

options.en: It was close enough to pick up without leaving the desk.
options.zh: 它近得不離開書桌就能拿起。

options.en: It was stored elsewhere and brought in only after the task.
options.zh: 它存放別處，工作完才拿來。

listening.explanationZh: beside notebook 及 without leaving desk 支持伸手可及，不等於全程拿在手。

reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼把參考卡放在筆記本旁？
reply.promptEn: Why did you put the reference card beside your notebook?

options.en: I could pick it up without leaving the desk.
options.zh: 我不離開書桌就可拿起它。

options.en: I wanted the card within arm’s reach.
options.zh: 我想把卡放在伸手可及的位置。

options.en: That position made it easy to consult during the task.
options.zh: 那位置讓我工作時容易查看。

options.en: I could reach it quickly when I needed a reminder.
options.zh: 需要提示時，我可以很快拿到它。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都解釋方便取用；金句直接描述伸手可及的位置。

scene.promptZh: 你坐着做筆記，需要間中查字典。哪個安排最符合 within arm’s reach？

options.en: The dictionary is beside your elbow on the desk.
options.zh: 字典在書桌上、手肘旁。

options.en: The dictionary is visible on the far wall shelf but requires you to stand and cross the room.
options.zh: 字典在遠牆架上看得見，但要起身走過房間才拿到。

options.en: The dictionary stays in a cupboard in the next room.
options.zh: 字典留在隔壁房間的櫃內。

scene.explanationZh: 手肘旁可直接伸手拿；可見而需走遠不同。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個說法把 within arm’s reach 誤解了？

options.en: It describes how easily the person can physically reach the object.
options.zh: 它描述人實際伸手取物的容易程度。

options.en: An object may be within arm’s reach without being held.
options.zh: 物件可以伸手可及，而未被拿在手中。

options.en: Any object in the same room qualifies, even if the person must walk over to it.
options.zh: 同一房間任何物件都算，即使人要走過去取。

contrast.explanationZh: 同房間不保證可伸手取，須看實際距離及位置。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友指着房間另一端的筆記說「看得見，所以 within arm’s reach」。哪句澄清最好？

options.en: Let us judge reach by visibility alone.
options.zh: 只按看不看得見判斷伸手距離吧。

options.en: You can see them, but you would need to move closer to pick them up.
options.zh: 你看得見，但要移近才拿得到。

options.en: Being in the same room is enough, so the distance from your seat does not matter.
options.zh: 在同一房間已足夠，所以離你座位的距離不重要。

dialogue.explanationZh: 可見與可伸手拿不同，需看人與物件的實際距離。

speaking.en: Keep your reference notes within arm’s reach while you work.
speaking.zh: 工作時把參考筆記放在伸手可及的位置。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再描述方便取用物件的安排。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：圖書館的故事角想讓年幼孩子自己選書，因此把常用繪本放在低籃，讓坐在小椅子的孩子伸手就拿到，不需成人代取。用一至兩句英文描述安排目的。

examples.en: The picture books are within arm’s reach in low baskets, so children can choose one without asking an adult to fetch it.
examples.zh: 繪本在低籃裏伸手可及，所以孩子可以自己選，不需成人代取。

examples.en: We put the favourite stories within arm’s reach of children seated in the reading corner, making independent choices easier.
examples.zh: 我們把喜愛故事放在閱讀角坐着的孩子伸手可及的位置，讓他們較易自己選。

writing.selfCheckZh: 從孩子坐着的位置說明能伸手取，而非只看書是否在同一房間或看得見。

takeaways.en: I keep a pencil within arm’s reach when I read.
takeaways.zh: 閱讀時我把鉛筆放在伸手可及的位置。

takeaways.en: A book can be visible without being within arm’s reach.
takeaways.zh: 書可以看得見，卻不在伸手可及的範圍。

brief.meaningEn: Actively look for a particular person, place, experience or thing, often making a deliberate effort.
brief.meaningZh: 主動、有意識地尋找特定的人、地方、經驗或事物，常要付出心力。
brief.grammar: seek out a person/place; seek someone out; past sought out; pronoun seek them out.
brief.register: Neutral English, slightly more deliberate than find.
brief.boundaryZh: 強調主動尋找，不是偶然遇到；不保證立即找到或選到最好的一個。
brief.misconceptionZh: 尋找不同意見可為了解，不表示已同意；尋找本身也不等於找到所有所需資料。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述有目的的搜尋及它與偶然遇上的差別。

listening.en: Rather than waiting for advice to arrive, the new gardener sought out experienced neighbours and asked about plants that suited the small balcony.
listening.zh: 新手園丁沒有等建議送上門，而是主動找有經驗鄰居，詢問適合小露台的植物。

options.en: They deliberately looked for experienced neighbours to ask.
options.zh: 他主動尋找有經驗的鄰居詢問。

options.en: They came across advice without trying to find anyone.
options.zh: 他沒嘗試找人，就偶然遇到建議。

options.en: They waited until a neighbour noticed the balcony problem.
options.zh: 他等到鄰居留意到露台問題。

options.en: They had already chosen plants before deciding whom to consult.
options.zh: 他決定問誰之前，已選定植物。

listening.explanationZh: rather than waiting 與 sought out 對比主動尋找和被動等待。

reply.promptZh: 你怎樣找到適合小露台的種植建議？
reply.promptEn: How did you find planting advice for your small balcony?

options.en: I asked around for neighbours with experience.
options.zh: 我四處詢問哪些鄰居有經驗。

options.en: I sought out experienced gardeners nearby.
options.zh: 我主動尋找附近有經驗的園丁。

options.en: I deliberately looked for someone who had grown plants in a small space.
options.zh: 我特意找曾在小空間種植的人。

options.en: I made an effort to find local people who could advise me.
options.zh: 我花心力找能給建議的本地人。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描述有目的地找人，而非偶然聽到；金句使用 sought out。

scene.promptZh: 你想了解一個街區的歷史，特意找住了多年的居民訪談。哪句最準確？

options.en: I waited for a history account to reach me without looking for anyone.
options.zh: 我沒有找人，只等歷史敘述送到我面前。

options.en: I stumbled upon a resident by chance and had no prior plan to ask.
options.zh: 我偶然碰到居民，事前無意詢問。

options.en: I sought out long-term residents to learn about the neighbourhood.
options.zh: 我主動找長期居民了解街區。

scene.explanationZh: 特意尋找受訪者是 seek out，與等候或無意遇到不同。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不像 seek out？

options.en: Searching for a specialist who can explain an unfamiliar technique.
options.zh: 尋找能解釋陌生技巧的專家。

options.en: Unexpectedly finding a useful booklet while cleaning a drawer, with no search planned.
options.zh: 整理抽屜時意外發現有用小冊子，原本沒有打算找。

options.en: Making visits to find examples of a local craft.
options.zh: 走訪尋找本地工藝的例子。

contrast.explanationZh: 未打算尋找卻意外發現，不具主動搜尋的重點。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說他 sought out 批評意見，別人便以為他已全部接受。哪句澄清最準確？

options.en: He looked for those views to understand them; he still needs to assess their reasons.
options.zh: 他找那些意見是為了了解；仍需評估理由。

options.en: Let us treat requesting criticism as accepting each suggested change.
options.zh: 把徵求批評當作接受每項修改吧。

options.en: The effort spent finding the advice is enough reason to accept it without review.
options.zh: 花了心力找建議，已足以作為不覆核就接受的理由。

dialogue.explanationZh: 主動找意見與認同意見不同，仍需評估內容。

speaking.en: We sought out local residents who could explain the area’s history.
speaking.zh: 我們主動找能解釋地區歷史的本地居民。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再描述為了特定目的主動找人。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你到一個陌生城鎮做速寫，不想只跟熱門景點路線，打算主動找安靜小院，細看日常建築。用一至兩句英文描述搜尋目的。

examples.en: I will seek out quiet courtyards where I can sketch ordinary buildings away from the main tourist route.
examples.zh: 我會主動尋找遠離主要遊客路線的安靜小院，在那裏速寫日常建築。

examples.en: Instead of following the busiest route, I will seek out small courtyards to observe local architecture more closely.
examples.zh: 我不會跟最繁忙路線，而會主動找小院，更仔細觀察本地建築。

writing.selfCheckZh: 說明有目的地找地方與想觀察甚麼，區分主動搜尋及偶然走進。

takeaways.en: She seeks out people with different experiences to broaden her understanding.
takeaways.zh: 她主動尋找有不同經歷的人，以擴闊理解。

takeaways.en: We sought out a quiet place where the group could talk.
takeaways.zh: 我們主動找一處讓小組交談的安靜地方。

brief.meaningEn: Become part of a routine or activity easily, sometimes with little conscious notice.
brief.meaningZh: 容易地成為習慣或活動的一部分，有時不知不覺就融入。
brief.grammar: slip (naturally) into a routine/daily life/a break; slipped is past. Taught only for integration into ordinary activity.
brief.register: A movement metaphor for easy integration.
brief.boundaryZh: naturally 強調順暢，quickly 強調速度；容易融入不必等於完全沒注意。不是身體滑倒，也不是本課以外的換衣等 slip into 用法。
brief.misconceptionZh: 順暢加入習慣不保證永遠維持，也不表示完全不用安排；需交代融入哪段生活。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述小活動或工具怎樣容易成為日常一部分，保留具體情境。

sources.sentence: New devices can slip into daily life very quickly.

listening.en: A ten-minute sketch slipped naturally into my lunch break because I already had a quiet few minutes after eating.
listening.zh: 十分鐘速寫自然融入我的午休，因為飯後本已有幾分鐘安靜時間。

options.en: The speaker stopped taking lunch breaks to make room for a long class.
options.zh: 說話者取消午休，騰出時間上長課。

options.en: The activity fitted easily into time already available after lunch.
options.zh: 活動容易融入午餐後原有的空檔。

options.en: The speaker planned it but never tried it during the break.
options.zh: 說話者計劃過，但從未在午休嘗試。

options.en: The sketching required the speaker to replace every other lunchtime activity.
options.zh: 速寫要求說話者取代午間每項其他活動。

listening.explanationZh: 已有安靜空檔讓十分鐘活動順暢加入；不是未開始或全面取代午休。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼你容易開始午間速寫？
reply.promptEn: Why was it easy for you to begin sketching at lunchtime?

options.en: It fitted the quiet time I already had after lunch.
options.zh: 它配合我午飯後本有的安靜時間。

options.en: The ten-minute activity fitted the quiet gap I already had after eating.
options.zh: 十分鐘活動配合我飯後原有的安靜空檔。

options.en: It slipped naturally into my lunch break.
options.zh: 它自然融入我的午休。

options.en: The short activity matched the gap in my usual routine.
options.zh: 這項短活動配合我平常習慣中的空檔。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都解釋容易加入的原因；金句使用順暢融入的比喻。

scene.promptZh: 你原本乘車前會等幾分鐘，現在用那段時間複習三張字卡，不需另騰長時段。哪句貼切？

options.en: A little revision has slipped into my usual waiting time.
options.zh: 少量複習已融入我平常的等候時間。

options.en: Revision has replaced the whole journey with a separate class.
options.zh: 複習已把整段旅程換成獨立課堂。

options.en: The waiting period remains unused because I have not begun revising.
options.zh: 我未開始複習，所以等候時間仍未使用。

scene.explanationZh: 原有空檔加入小活動支持融入習慣，不是獨立長課或未開始。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不像活動已 slip into a routine？

options.en: A short habit becomes a regular part of an existing break.
options.zh: 短習慣成為原有休息時段的固定部分。

options.en: A useful tool becomes an ordinary part of preparing the daily journey.
options.zh: 有用工具成為每日出行準備的普通一部分。

options.en: A proposed activity remains outside the routine because no time has been found for it.
options.zh: 因未找到時間，建議活動仍未加入生活習慣。

contrast.explanationZh: 仍未加入與已容易融入相反；關鍵是成為日常部分。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「速寫 slips naturally into 午休，所以我完全不用準備材料」。哪句回應最準確？

options.en: Let us treat a good fit with the schedule as proof that supplies are unnecessary.
options.zh: 把配合時間表當作不需用品的證據吧。

options.en: It can fit easily into the break, and keeping the materials ready can still help.
options.zh: 它可以容易融入午休，同時預備好材料仍有幫助。

options.en: Its short duration means we can skip arranging the materials.
options.zh: 它時間短，表示可以不安排材料。

dialogue.explanationZh: 融入時間與材料準備是不同需要；naturally 不代表毋須安排。

speaking.en: A short walk slips naturally into the quiet part of my afternoon.
speaking.zh: 短散步自然融入我下午安靜的一段時間。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再描述短活動怎樣融入原有生活。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你原本只試用一個電子車票工具，後來上學通勤及周末探訪都自然用到，不知不覺成為日常一部分。用一至兩句英文描述融入，不假設它適合所有人。

examples.en: The ticket app slipped into my daily life as I used it for both the school journey and weekend visits.
examples.zh: 我用車票工具上學及周末探訪時，它逐漸自然融入我的日常生活。

examples.en: What began as a trial slipped naturally into my travel routine because it covered several journeys I already made.
examples.zh: 原本只是試用，後來自然融入我的出行習慣，因為它配合我本來已有的幾段路程。

glossary.zh: 我本來已有的幾段路程

writing.selfCheckZh: 用不同原有路程中的實際採用支持容易融入，不只說試過一次，也不推成所有人都適用。

takeaways.en: A useful map app can slip into daily life as part of planning a journey.
takeaways.zh: 有用地圖應用程式可以融入日常，成為出行規劃的一部分。

takeaways.en: A short reading habit slipped naturally into her evening routine.
takeaways.zh: 短閱讀習慣自然融入她晚間的生活。

titleEn: on the spur of the moment

brief.meaningEn: Spontaneously, without having planned the action in advance.
brief.meaningZh: 事前未有計劃，當下自發作出決定或行動。
brief.grammar: decide/do something on the spur of the moment; fixed phrase.
brief.register: Common conversational idiom.
brief.boundaryZh: 說明沒有預先安排，不自動等於魯莽、後悔或成功；人可以當下查看可行性再決定。
brief.misconceptionZh: 臨近出發才作決定與事前已定好不同；偶然遇見不等於自己決定行動。
brief.outcomeZh: 能區分預定安排與即興決定，避免從未預先計劃推斷結果。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.expression: on the spur of the moment
sources.sentence: We decided to visit the gallery on the spur of the moment.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 2, table 2, row 5; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: We saw that the small gallery was still open and decided on the spur of the moment to go in; it had not been part of our afternoon plan.
listening.zh: 我們看到小畫廊仍開放，就一時興起決定進去；它原不在下午計劃中。
listening.promptZh: 參觀畫廊是怎樣決定的？

options.en: They had reserved the whole afternoon for it several weeks earlier.
options.zh: 他們幾星期前已為此預留整個下午。

options.en: They made an unplanned decision after noticing it was open.
options.zh: 他們留意到仍開放後，作了事前未安排的決定。

options.en: They had planned it but cancelled after seeing the opening hours.
options.zh: 他們原有計劃，看到開放時間後取消。

options.en: They entered only because the earlier booking required it.
options.zh: 他們只因較早的預約要求而進去。

listening.explanationZh: not part of plan 與當下看見開放支持即興決定，不表示早已預約。

reply.promptZh: 你們有預先安排下午參觀畫廊嗎？
reply.promptEn: Had you planned the gallery visit before that afternoon?

options.en: No, we chose to go in only after seeing it was open.
options.zh: 沒有，看到仍開放後我們才決定進去。

options.en: No, it was not part of the plan we started with.
options.zh: 沒有，它原不在我們最初的計劃中。

options.en: No, we decided on the spur of the moment.
options.zh: 沒有，我們是一時興起決定的。

options.en: No, the idea came to us as we were passing.
options.zh: 沒有，我們經過時才想到。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都否定預先安排並交代臨時起意；金句用固定片語。

scene.promptZh: 你和朋友原只打算散步，經過公園見有空座位，就即時決定看一場免費表演。哪句準確？

options.en: We had scheduled this performance before arranging the walk.
options.zh: 安排散步前，我們已排定看這場表演。

options.en: We decided on the spur of the moment to watch the performance.
options.zh: 我們一時興起決定看表演。

options.en: We kept our earlier booking for the performance despite planning to leave.
options.zh: 雖然打算離開，我們仍履行較早預約。

scene.explanationZh: 經過才決定與預訂不同；題目沒有先前安排。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項資料最不符合 on the spur of the moment？

options.en: The choice was first made while they were already nearby.
options.zh: 他們已在附近時才首次作出選擇。

options.en: They had not intended to do it earlier that day.
options.zh: 當天較早時，他們沒有這個打算。

options.en: The exact activity had been booked and agreed a month earlier.
options.zh: 確切活動在一個月前已預約及議定。

contrast.explanationZh: 一個月前已訂好是提前計劃，不是當下自發決定。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「on the spur of the moment，所以那一定是壞決定」。哪句澄清最好？

options.en: It tells us the decision was unplanned, not whether the outcome was good or bad.
options.zh: 它告訴我們決定未預先安排，不是結果好壞。

options.en: Let us judge the outcome from the timing of the decision alone.
options.zh: 只按作決定的時間判斷結果吧。

options.en: It must have been an accident rather than a choice, since it was not planned.
options.zh: 既然未預先計劃，就必定是意外，而非自己選擇。

dialogue.explanationZh: 即興描述計劃程度，評估好壞還需其他證據。

speaking.en: We decided on the spur of the moment to stay for the short concert.
speaking.zh: 我們一時興起決定留下看短音樂會。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再描述原先未安排的即時決定。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你原定回家直接吃現成晚餐，看到鄰居送來的新鮮蔬菜後，當下決定和室友一起煮，事前沒有安排。用一至兩句英文描述決定。

examples.en: We decided on the spur of the moment to cook together after the neighbour brought fresh vegetables.
examples.zh: 鄰居送來新鮮蔬菜後，我們一時興起決定一起煮飯。

examples.en: Cooking had not been in our plan, but we chose on the spur of the moment to make dinner with the vegetables we had just received.
examples.zh: 煮飯原不在計劃中，但我們一時興起，決定用剛收到的蔬菜做晚餐。

writing.selfCheckZh: 明確原未安排、收到蔬菜後才決定，不把即興自動評價為魯莽或成功。

takeaways.en: They booked a short trip on the spur of the moment.
takeaways.zh: 他們一時興起預訂了短旅行。

takeaways.en: A choice made on the spur of the moment can still turn out well.
takeaways.zh: 一時興起作出的選擇，結果仍可以很好。

brief.meaningEn: Firmly integrated into ordinary routines and activities.
brief.meaningZh: 穩固地融入平常習慣與活動之中。
brief.grammar: be/become embedded in daily life; embedded is figurative integration, not a physical object inserted in material.
brief.register: Descriptive metaphor, often about practices or technology.
brief.boundaryZh: 需有反覆日常使用或參與，不是只出現一次；不保證每個人都用、永遠不變或全無缺點。
brief.misconceptionZh: 廣告常見不等於活動已融入使用者生活；要看實際日常角色。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用平常活動的具體例子支持已成為日常一部分。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Digital maps are embedded in daily life for many travellers.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 2, table 2, row 6; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: For this family, checking the shared calendar is embedded in daily life: they use it each morning to coordinate school, work and visits.
listening.zh: 對這家庭而言，查看共用日曆已融入日常：他們每天早上用它協調上學、工作與探訪。
listening.promptZh: 甚麼顯示日曆已融入這家庭的生活？

options.en: They saw an advertisement but have not tried the calendar.
options.zh: 他們看過廣告，但未試用日曆。

options.en: They use it for a one-off demonstration unrelated to their plans.
options.zh: 他們只在與生活計劃無關的一次示範中使用它。

options.en: They use it regularly to coordinate ordinary activities.
options.zh: 他們定期用它協調平常活動。

options.en: They stopped using it before it could affect the morning routine.
options.zh: 它影響早上習慣前，他們已停止使用。

listening.explanationZh: 每天協調上學、工作及探訪是實際日常角色，不只是看廣告。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼你說共用日曆已是這家庭生活的一部分？
reply.promptEn: Why do you say the shared calendar is part of this family’s ordinary life?

options.en: They check it every morning before arranging the day.
options.zh: 他們每天早上安排當天活動前都查看。

options.en: Daily coordination of school and work shows it is embedded in their daily life.
options.zh: 每天協調上學與工作，顯示它已融入他們日常生活。

options.en: It regularly connects their school, work and family plans.
options.zh: 它定期連繫他們的上學、工作與家庭計劃。

options.en: They depend on the routine of checking it together.
options.zh: 他們靠着一起查看的習慣作安排。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以日常整合回應；金句使用 embedded 的比喻。

scene.promptZh: 同學已習慣每天用錄音記事整理採訪、回顧及分工，不只在介紹會試用一次。哪句貼切？

options.en: The recording practice is embedded in their daily life.
options.zh: 錄音記事的做法已融入他們的日常生活。

options.en: The practice remains an unused idea from the introductory session.
options.zh: 這做法仍是介紹會中未用過的構想。

options.en: Its only role was a single demonstration before the students abandoned it.
options.zh: 它只在學生放棄前的一次示範發揮作用。

scene.explanationZh: 每天整合不同任務顯示實際融入，與只示範或未用不同。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項資料最不足以單獨支持 embedded in daily life？

options.en: People use the practice in several ordinary routines.
options.zh: 人們在幾項平常習慣中運用這做法。

options.en: A display introduces the tool once, with no evidence of later use.
options.zh: 展示只介紹工具一次，沒有之後使用的證據。

options.en: The activity is a familiar part of daily preparation.
options.zh: 活動是每日準備中熟悉的一部分。

contrast.explanationZh: 一次介紹不能單獨支持已成為穩固日常習慣。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友見到工具廣告到處都是，便說它 embedded in daily life。哪句追問最有幫助？

options.en: The frequency of the adverts establishes how often people actually use it.
options.zh: 廣告頻率已確定人們實際使用頻率。

options.en: A single trial is enough to establish that the tool is part of a regular routine.
options.zh: 只試用一次，已足以確定工具成為固定習慣一部分。

options.en: How do people actually use it in their ordinary routines?
options.zh: 人們實際怎樣在平常習慣中使用它？

dialogue.explanationZh: 要看平常反覆實際使用；廣告頻率或一次試用不能代替日常採用的證據。

speaking.en: Checking the shared calendar is embedded in our daily life.
speaking.zh: 查看共用日曆已融入我們的日常生活。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再描述穩定日常習慣。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：一個雙語家庭平常用兩種語言讀食譜、跟長輩聊天及解釋功課，不只在語言課才切換。用一至兩句英文描述雙語交流與日常的關係。

examples.en: Using two languages is embedded in our daily life, from family conversations to recipes and homework explanations.
examples.zh: 使用兩種語言已融入我們的日常生活，從家庭交談到食譜與功課解釋都是。

examples.en: Bilingual communication is embedded in daily life in this household; it connects ordinary tasks as well as conversations with older relatives.
examples.zh: 雙語交流已融入這家庭日常；它連繫平常工作，也連繫與長輩的交談。

writing.selfCheckZh: 用多種日常交流活動支持穩固融合，不只列一次語言課，也不把某家庭推及所有家庭。

takeaways.en: Shared reading is embedded in daily life in that household.
takeaways.zh: 共同閱讀已融入那個家庭的日常生活。

takeaways.en: A practice can be embedded in daily life and still change as people’s needs change.
takeaways.zh: 做法可以深融日常，仍隨人們需要改變。

brief.meaningEn: Have a lasting or noticeable effect; strong and deep emphasise degree, while lasting emphasises duration.

brief.grammar: leave a strong/deep/lasting mark on + person/community/development; past left. Leave their/your/our/its mark on something is the possessive variant. Lasting evaluates duration, not a separate physical mark.
brief.register: Transparent mark metaphor; strong evaluates impact, not necessarily praise.
brief.boundaryZh: 影響可正可負，並非實際污漬；需有後續作用，不只是當下注意。
brief.misconceptionZh: 持久影響不表示是唯一原因，也不表示人的未來不能再改變。
brief.outcomeZh: 能以後來的習慣或發展支持長遠影響，避免單一原因推斷。

listening.en: The patient debate coach left a strong mark on me: years later, I still pause to consider opposing views before I answer.
listening.zh: 耐心的辯論教練對我留下深遠影響：多年後，回答前我仍會停下來考慮相反觀點。
listening.promptZh: 甚麼支持教練有長遠影響？

options.en: The coach made a brief impression, but the speaker soon stopped using the discussion habit.
options.zh: 教練帶來短暫印象，但說話者很快不再用該討論習慣。

options.en: The speaker still uses a habit learned from the coach years later.
options.zh: 多年後，說話者仍運用從教練學到的習慣。

options.en: The speaker forgot the advice immediately after the lesson.
options.zh: 說話者課後立即忘記建議。

options.en: The coach’s advice was planned but never given.
options.zh: 教練的建議曾計劃給出，但從未提出。

listening.explanationZh: years later 與仍先考慮反方顯示後續持久作用，不只是即時注意。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼你說那位教練影響你很深？
reply.promptEn: Why do you say that coach influenced you deeply?

options.en: I still use the discussion habit she taught me years ago.
options.zh: 我仍用她多年前教的討論習慣。

options.en: Her guidance continues to shape how I answer opposing views.
options.zh: 她的指導仍影響我回應相反觀點的方式。

options.en: She left a strong mark: I still consider opposing views as she taught me.
options.zh: 她留下深遠影響：我仍按她所教，先考慮相反觀點。

options.en: I have carried her patient approach into later conversations.
options.zh: 我把她耐心的方法帶到後來的對話中。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都提供持續作用；金句用留下痕跡的比喻。

scene.promptZh: 一次社區合作經驗讓你學會先聽居民意見，幾年後做新計劃仍沿用。哪句最有根據？

options.en: The experience left a strong mark on how I plan community projects.
options.zh: 那次經驗對我規劃社區項目的方式留下深遠影響。

options.en: The experience held my attention briefly but had no later effect on my planning.
options.zh: 那次經驗短暫吸引我注意，之後沒有影響規劃。

options.en: The experience remains only a proposal I have not taken part in.
options.zh: 那次經驗仍只是我尚未參與的提案。

scene.explanationZh: 幾年後沿用方法支持長遠影響，與短暫注意不同。

contrast.promptZh: 哪句把 leave a strong mark 推論得過頭？

options.en: A later habit can be evidence of a lasting effect.
options.zh: 後來的習慣可作持久影響的證據。

options.en: The effect must be the only cause of everything the person later does.
options.zh: 該影響必須是當事人之後所有行為的唯一原因。

options.en: The lasting effect may be helpful or harmful depending on the experience.
options.zh: 長遠影響可依經驗而有益或有害。

contrast.explanationZh: 強烈持久不等於唯一原因，也不自動評價正面或負面。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「那次失望 left a strong mark，所以我再不可能改變做事方式」。哪句回應最好？

options.en: Decline the new opportunity without finding out whether it differs from the old one.
options.zh: 未了解新機會是否與舊經歷不同，就先拒絕。

options.en: Keep the old approach without reviewing whether it fits the new situation.
options.zh: 不檢視是否適合新情況，就保持舊方法。

options.en: That disappointment left a strong mark, but new experiences can also change your approach.
options.zh: 那次失望留下了深遠影響，但新經驗也可以改變你的做法。

dialogue.explanationZh: 回應承認過往失望留下影響，也沒有斷言它是唯一影響或未來不能改變；仍可了解新機會及檢視方法。

speaking.en: That patient teacher left a strong mark on how I support younger learners.
speaking.zh: 那位耐心老師對我支持年幼學習者的方式留下深遠影響。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明過往人物如何持續影響現在。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：早年的小組項目因分工不清失敗，幾年後你做新項目仍會先寫清角色及交接。用一至兩句英文描述那次經驗的持續影響，不說它是唯一原因。

examples.en: The failed group project left a strong mark on how I organise work; years later, I still clarify roles before we begin.
examples.zh: 失敗的小組項目對我安排工作的方式留下深遠影響；多年後，我仍在開始前釐清角色。

examples.en: That experience left a strong mark on my planning habits, and I now write down responsibilities and handovers for each project.
examples.zh: 那次經驗對我的規劃習慣留下深遠影響，我現在每個項目都寫下責任與交接。

writing.selfCheckZh: 用多年後仍改變做法支持持久影響，容許負面經驗帶來學習，不把它說成未來唯一原因。

takeaways.en: The difficult year left a strong mark on the community.
takeaways.zh: 艱難的一年對社區留下深遠影響。

takeaways.en: The library's weekly visits left a lasting mark on how the children read at home.
takeaways.zh: 圖書館每週到訪，長久影響孩子們在家閱讀的方式。

brief.meaningEn: Music or sound that regularly accompanies ordinary activities or a life period and becomes strongly associated with those experiences.
brief.meaningZh: 經常陪伴平常活動或一段人生時期，並讓人把聲音與那些經歷連在一起的音樂或聲響。
brief.grammar: become/be the soundtrack of everyday life or the soundtrack of a whole period of life; soundtrack borrows the music-track idea from films. The first highlights recurring routines, the second association with a life stage.
brief.register: A speaker recalling a familiar routine or life stage to a friend can use this creative but understandable sound metaphor.
brief.boundaryZh: 不表示生活真的被拍成電影，也不必全天播放或每人聽相同音樂；要有平常活動或人生時期與聲音反覆連繫的線索。
brief.misconceptionZh: 一次音樂會不自動成為日常背景或整段人生的代表；需要可辨認的重複經驗。
brief.outcomeZh: 能把常聽聲音連結到通勤、煮食等例行活動，或一段人生時期。

listening.en: For my family, the morning radio has become the soundtrack of everyday life, playing while we make breakfast and get ready to leave.
listening.zh: 對我家而言，早晨收音機已成為日常生活的背景樂，在做早餐與準備出門時播放。
listening.promptZh: 收音機在這家庭有甚麼角色？

options.en: It provides sound for a film they are recording about one unusual day.
options.zh: 它為他們拍攝某個特別日子的電影提供聲音。

options.en: It plays only during a single planned performance.
options.zh: 它只在一場預定表演期間播放。

options.en: It regularly accompanies ordinary morning activities.
options.zh: 它經常陪伴平常的早上活動。

options.en: It has replaced breakfast preparation as the family’s main daily task.
options.zh: 它已取代準備早餐，成為家庭每日主要工作。

listening.explanationZh: 做早餐與出門準備是反覆生活情境，soundtrack 是比喻陪伴。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼早晨電台讓你想到家裏平常的生活？
reply.promptEn: Why does the morning radio remind you of ordinary life at home?

options.en: We hear it while preparing breakfast most mornings.
options.zh: 大多數早上準備早餐時，我們都聽到它。

options.en: It is the soundtrack of everyday life in our kitchen.
options.zh: 它是我們廚房日常生活的背景樂。

options.en: Its familiar programmes accompany our usual morning routine.
options.zh: 它熟悉的節目陪伴我們平常早上的習慣。

options.en: I associate those voices with getting ready to leave home.
options.zh: 我把那些聲音與準備出門連在一起。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以日常聲音陪伴解釋聯想；金句用電影聲軌作生活比喻。

scene.promptZh: 你每天通勤都聽一份熟悉歌單，前奏常令你想到車窗外平常路線。哪句貼切？

options.en: The playlist has become the soundtrack of everyday life on my commute.
options.zh: 歌單已成為我通勤日常的背景樂。

options.en: The playlist is only a sound effect for a one-off theatre rehearsal.
options.zh: 歌單只是一次劇院彩排的音效。

options.en: The playlist is a new recording I have never played during a journey.
options.zh: 歌單是我旅途中從未播放的新錄音。

scene.explanationZh: 每天通勤的重複陪伴支持日常背景樂，不是只一次或從未使用。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不足以支持 the soundtrack of everyday life？

options.en: A familiar broadcast accompanies breakfast repeatedly.
options.zh: 熟悉廣播反覆陪伴早餐。

options.en: A song is heard once at a special ceremony, with no connection to ordinary routines described.
options.zh: 歌曲只在特別典禮聽過一次，沒有描述與平常習慣的連結。

options.en: A regular playlist becomes closely associated with the journey to work.
options.zh: 固定歌單與上班路程建立密切聯想。

contrast.explanationZh: 只一次特別典禮不足以支持日常陪伴，需普通重複活動。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「只有一場正式音樂會的配樂，才可叫日常生活的聲軌」。哪句澄清最準確？

options.en: A single concert automatically defines the sounds of the family’s whole routine.
options.zh: 一場音樂會自動定義整個家庭日常的聲音。

options.en: We should leave the familiar kitchen radio out unless it was written for a film.
options.zh: 除非是為電影創作，否則應把熟悉廚房電台聲音排除。

options.en: Familiar kitchen radio can be the soundtrack of everyday life even without a formal concert or film.
options.zh: 熟悉的廚房電台聲音也可成為日常生活的背景樂，不需要正式音樂會或電影。

dialogue.explanationZh: 日常聲軌是比喻平常反覆陪伴的聲音，不需正式音樂會或真正電影配樂。

speaking.en: The kitchen radio is the soundtrack of everyday life in our home.
speaking.zh: 廚房收音機是我們家日常生活的背景樂。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再把熟悉聲音連結到生活習慣。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你住在熱鬧街區，早上常聽到檔販叫賣、自行車鈴及店舖開門聲；這些並非歌曲，卻與你每天上學的路連在一起。用一至兩句英文用聲軌比喻描述。

examples.en: Market calls and bicycle bells are the soundtrack of everyday life on my walk to school.
examples.zh: 叫賣聲與自行車鈴聲是我上學路上日常生活的聲軌。

examples.en: The familiar sounds of stalls opening have become the soundtrack of everyday life in our neighbourhood, even without music.
examples.zh: 攤檔開張的熟悉聲響，即使不是音樂，也已成為我們社區日常生活的聲軌。

writing.selfCheckZh: 用反覆上學路上的非音樂聲音支持生活聲軌比喻，不說真的拍了電影。

takeaways.zh: 她在修讀建築期間深夜畫圖常聽的歌單，成為那段人生的背景樂。

brief.meaningEn: Feel satisfaction and a sense of value in an achievement, quality, work or connection.
brief.meaningZh: 對成就、特質、工作或所屬連結感到滿足及重視。

listening.en: The residents take pride in their shared garden and still welcome suggestions about making it easier for more neighbours to use.
listening.zh: 居民以共用花園為榮，仍歡迎讓更多鄰居方便使用的建議。
listening.promptZh: 居民的自豪與回饋是甚麼關係？

options.en: They value the garden while remaining open to improvements.
options.zh: 他們重視花園，同時願意改進。

options.en: They reject suggestions because satisfaction means nothing can change.
options.zh: 他們拒絕建議，因為滿足代表不能改動。

options.en: They feel ashamed of contributing to the garden.
options.zh: 他們對參與花園感到羞恥。

options.en: They are proud only of a private space that neighbours cannot share.
options.zh: 他們只以鄰居不能共用的私人空間為榮。

reply.promptZh: 居民對一起建立的花園有甚麼感受？
reply.promptEn: How do the residents feel about the garden they created together?

options.en: They are pleased with what they have created together.
options.zh: 他們滿意一起建立的成果。

options.en: They take pride in the shared garden.
options.zh: 他們以共用花園為榮。

options.en: They value the garden as a worthwhile community achievement.
options.zh: 他們重視花園，視它為有價值的社區成果。

options.en: They feel a positive sense of ownership and care for it.
options.zh: 他們有正面的歸屬感，並用心照顧它。

scene.promptZh: 同學用心修訂刊物，對共同成果滿意，也請讀者指出可改進的地方。哪句貼切？

options.en: They dismiss the magazine as having no value despite their effort.
options.zh: 雖然付出心力，他們仍認為刊物毫無價值。

options.en: They regard reader suggestions as proof that the publication has failed completely.
options.zh: 他們把讀者建議視為刊物徹底失敗的證據。

options.en: They take pride in the magazine while welcoming useful feedback.
options.zh: 他們以刊物為榮，同時歡迎有用回饋。

scene.explanationZh: 滿意共同成果與願意修訂相容，不是毫無價值或徹底失敗。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論最不宜由 take pride in their work 得出？

options.zh: 他們重視工作的品質或成果。

options.en: They must regard other people as inferior and refuse all criticism.
options.zh: 他們必定把別人視作低人一等，並拒絕所有批評。

options.en: They may put care into how the work is done.

contrast.explanationZh: 自豪不等於輕視別人或拒絕回饋。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「你 take pride in 刊物，怎能再請人指出問題？」哪句回應最好？

options.en: We can value our work and still use feedback to improve it.
options.zh: 我們可以重視作品，同時用回饋改善它。

options.en: Ask reviewers only for praise so the group’s pride is not challenged.
options.zh: 只請覆核者讚賞，免得挑戰小組的自豪。

options.en: Feeling pleased with the draft is enough to conclude that it needs no further checking.
options.zh: 對草稿滿意，已足以斷定不需再查核。

dialogue.explanationZh: 重視成果與持續改善可以並行；滿足不取代查核。

speaking.en: We take pride in our work and welcome ideas for making it better.
speaking.zh: 我們以工作為榮，也歡迎令它更好的想法。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再把自豪與願意改善連在一起。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：跑步比賽你沒有拿獎，但訓練後的個人時間有進步；你重視用心準備，仍想聽教練建議。用一至兩句英文表達自豪與改善。

examples.en: I take pride in the effort behind my improved time, even without a medal, and I still welcome my coach’s advice.
examples.zh: 即使沒有獎牌，我仍以改善時間背後的努力為榮，也歡迎教練建議。

examples.en: Taking pride in my preparation does not mean I think the race was perfect; I want feedback on how to improve further.
examples.zh: 以準備為榮不代表認為比賽完美；我想聽怎樣繼續進步的回饋。

writing.selfCheckZh: 以具體努力及時間進步為榮，不把自豪限於得獎，也保留接受改善意見。

sources.sentence: Bright pictures catch people's attention quickly.

listening.en: The unusual opening rhythm caught listeners’ attention, and several people stopped talking to hear what came next.
listening.zh: 特別的開場節奏吸引了聽眾注意，幾個人停止交談，聽接下來的內容。
listening.promptZh: 甚麼顯示節奏吸引了注意？

options.en: People stopped talking and began listening.
options.zh: 人們停止交談並開始聆聽。

options.en: The audience had already agreed with every point before hearing it.
options.zh: 觀眾未聽內容已同意每項觀點。

options.en: The rhythm made people leave without noticing the performance.
options.zh: 節奏讓人沒留意演出就離開。

options.en: The listeners later recalled the full piece accurately, rather than merely beginning to attend to it.
options.zh: 聽眾之後準確記得整首作品，而不只是開始留意。

listening.explanationZh: 停止交談並聽後文是注意轉移的證據，不是已理解或同意全部內容。

reply.promptZh: 那段特別節奏有甚麼即時效果？
reply.promptEn: What immediate effect did the unusual rhythm have?

options.en: It made people pause their conversations and listen.
options.zh: 它讓人停下交談，開始聆聽。

options.en: It caught listeners’ attention.
options.zh: 它吸引了聽眾注意。

options.en: People noticed the opening and wanted to hear more.
options.zh: 人們留意到開場，想繼續聽。

options.en: It drew the room’s focus to the performance.
options.zh: 它把現場的注意力帶到演出。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描述即時注意；金句用自然 attention 搭配。

scene.promptZh: 你用一句清楚而出乎意料的問題開始廣播，原本分心的同學抬頭聽。哪句有根據？

options.en: The question caught listeners’ attention at the start.
options.zh: 問題在開場吸引了聽眾注意。

options.en: The question settled every listener’s opinion on the topic.
options.zh: 問題已決定每位聽眾對議題的看法。

options.en: The question went unnoticed while the listeners continued their other conversations.
options.zh: 聽眾繼續別的交談，未留意問題。

scene.explanationZh: 抬頭聽支持開始注意，不足以判定立場或全部內容的理解。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項結論超出了 catch listeners’ attention？

options.en: People begin noticing the sound or message.
options.zh: 人們開始注意聲音或信息。

options.en: A distinctive opening may draw interest.
options.zh: 特別的開場可能引起興趣。

options.en: Noticing the opening proves lasting agreement with the whole message.
options.zh: 留意開場證明對整段信息長期贊同。

contrast.explanationZh: 注意是開始聽；全面及長期贊同需要另外證據。

dialogue.promptZh: 同學說「開場 caught listeners’ attention，所以他們一定已明白結論」。哪句澄清最好？

options.en: Their attention is enough preparation for the next task, so we can skip the still-needed explanation.
options.zh: 他們留意已足以準備下一項工作，所以可省略仍需要的解釋。

options.en: Their interest in the opening lets us report that they understood the whole argument.
options.zh: 他們對開場有興趣，讓我們可報稱他們明白整個論點。

options.en: The opening caught listeners’ attention, but we still need to explain the conclusion clearly and check what they understood.
options.zh: 開場吸引了聽眾注意，但我們仍需清楚解釋結論，並查核他們理解了甚麼。

dialogue.explanationZh: 注意轉移是開端，不等於準備已足夠或已理解整個論點；仍需清楚解釋並查核。

speaking.en: The short opening question caught listeners’ attention.
speaking.zh: 簡短開場問題吸引了聽眾注意。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再描述開場帶來的注意轉移。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：演講中段大家低頭翻筆記，講者短暫停頓，聽眾抬頭留意接下來的話。你只能確認注意轉移，還未知是否同意。用一至兩句英文描述。

examples.en: The brief pause caught listeners’ attention, and people looked up from their notes to hear what came next.
examples.zh: 短暫停頓吸引了聽眾注意，人們從筆記抬頭聽接下來的話。

examples.en: Silence in the middle of the talk caught listeners’ attention, but it did not tell us whether they agreed with the argument.
examples.zh: 演講中段的安靜吸引了聽眾注意，但沒有告訴我們他們是否同意論點。

glossary.en: in the middle of the talk

writing.selfCheckZh: 用抬頭聽支持注意轉移，這次由安靜而非大聲開場引起；不要推論已同意。

takeaways.en: A distinctive voice can catch listeners’ attention.
takeaways.zh: 有特色的聲音可以吸引聽眾注意。

takeaways.en: A single bold photograph can catch people’s attention before they read the safety notice.
takeaways.zh: 一張醒目的照片可先吸引人們注意，然後他們才閱讀安全告示。

titleZh: 被擠到邊緣而少被重視

brief.meaningEn: Made less visible, influential or central in an activity or discussion.
brief.meaningZh: 在活動或討論中變得較少被看見、較少影響力或較不受重視。
brief.grammar: Be pushed (quietly) to the margins or to the sidelines of a debate, programme or cultural space; both spatial metaphors describe lost prominence or influence, not literal seating. The adverb can describe a gradual or low-profile loss of attention.
brief.register: Figurative social or organisational description. A curator may tell colleagues that smaller art forms are being pushed quietly to the margins when their programme slots and publicity shrink.
brief.boundaryZh: 不一定完全被排除或實際坐在邊位；需說清參與、注意或影響力減少的證據。
brief.misconceptionZh: 仍在場不代表仍有實質參與；反過來，未採用一個建議也不單獨證明整個群體被邊緣化。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用發言機會、議程或資源的具體變化描述邊緣化。

sources.sentence: Local artists should not be pushed to the sidelines.

listening.en: When the agenda gave almost all the time to large organisations, the small volunteer groups were pushed to the margins and had little chance to explain their needs.
listening.zh: 議程把幾乎全部時間給大機構時，小義工團體被擠到邊緣，少有機會解釋需要。
listening.promptZh: 小團體的主要困難是甚麼？

options.en: They chose to lead the discussion and set every agenda item.
options.zh: 它們選擇主導討論，訂定每項議程。

options.en: They attended but had little opportunity to make their needs heard.
options.zh: 它們出席，但少有機會讓需要被聽到。

options.en: They were the only groups given time to speak.
options.zh: 只有它們獲發言時間。

options.en: They rejected an equal speaking allocation because they wanted a shorter meeting.
options.zh: 它們因想縮短會議而拒絕平等發言分配。

listening.explanationZh: little chance to explain 提供實質參與減少的證據，不只是座位位置。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼小義工團體覺得難以參與這次討論？
reply.promptEn: Why did the small volunteer groups find it hard to participate?

options.en: They had very little speaking time.
options.zh: 它們的發言時間很少。

options.en: The agenda gave their needs little attention.
options.zh: 議程很少注意它們的需要。

options.en: They were pushed to the margins of the discussion.
options.zh: 它們被擠到討論邊緣。

options.en: The larger organisations took nearly all the available time.
options.zh: 大機構佔去幾乎全部可用時間。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都解釋參與機會少；金句用邊緣意象。

scene.promptZh: 社團仍邀年幼會員出席，但長期不給他們發言，也不把他們的需要列入議程。哪句最有根據？

options.en: The younger members have been pushed to the margins of decision-making.
options.zh: 年幼會員被擠到決策邊緣。

options.en: The invitation alone shows that they have an equal voice in decisions.
options.zh: 單憑獲邀已顯示他們在決策有平等發言權。

options.en: They are setting the agenda and directing the older members’ contributions.
options.zh: 他們正訂議程並指揮年長會員發言。

scene.explanationZh: 出席與實質參與不同；長期未能發言及列需要支持邊緣化。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項資料最不足以單獨支持 pushed to the margins？

options.en: A group repeatedly receives little time to explain its needs.
options.zh: 一個團體反覆少有時間解釋需要。

options.en: A proposal is considered carefully but not chosen, while the group keeps an equal voice.
options.zh: 提案被仔細考慮後未獲選，但團體仍有平等發言權。

options.en: The agenda regularly leaves a group’s concerns unaddressed.
options.zh: 議程經常不處理某團體的關切。

contrast.explanationZh: 一次有理由未採納不單獨表示整體影響力被壓低。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「他們仍在會場，就不可能 pushed to the margins」。哪句回應最準確？

options.en: Let us use attendance alone to measure influence.
options.zh: 只用出席衡量影響力吧。

options.en: Being present does not rule out being pushed to the margins; check how much time or influence they actually have.
options.zh: 人在場仍可能被推到邊緣；要查他們實際有多少發言時間或影響力。

options.en: An invitation is enough evidence that their needs reached the agenda.
options.zh: 單憑邀請，已有足夠證據顯示他們的需要列入議程。

dialogue.explanationZh: 需要看發言、議程及影響，不只看有沒有到場。

speaking.en: Smaller groups should not be pushed to the margins of the discussion.
speaking.zh: 較小團體不應被擠到討論邊緣。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再表達實質參與的重要。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：一部社區歷史短片反覆訪問知名訪客，卻很少呈現長期居民的經驗，居民覺得自己的故事不被看見。用一至兩句英文指出問題並建議補充訪談。

examples.en: Long-term residents are being pushed to the margins of the film while famous visitors receive most of the attention. We should include more local interviews.
examples.zh: 知名訪客獲大部分注意時，長期居民正被擠到短片邊緣。我們應加入更多本地訪談。

examples.en: The residents’ stories have been pushed to the margins, so the next edit should give their experiences a clearer place.
examples.zh: 居民故事被擠到邊緣，所以下次剪輯應讓他們的經驗更清楚呈現。

writing.selfCheckZh: 描述呈現與注意分配的證據，提出讓故事可見的改動，不只看居民有沒有到拍攝現場。

takeaways.en: Local concerns were pushed to the margins of the wider debate.
takeaways.zh: 本地關切被擠到較大辯論的邊緣。

takeaways.en: Small theatre groups can be pushed to the sidelines when a festival cuts their stage time.
takeaways.zh: 當節慶削減小劇團的演出時間，它們可能被擠到邊緣。

brief.meaningEn: Produce a pleasing, impressive or seemingly special effect, often without each detail being explained.
brief.meaningZh: 產生悅人、令人印象深刻或彷彿神奇的效果，常未逐項解釋過程。
brief.grammar: something works its magic on someone/something; past worked; not a claim of supernatural power.
brief.register: Informal approving idiom; the exact effect depends on context.
brief.boundaryZh: 可形容花園、音樂或手藝效果，不保證每個人同樣反應；本課的放鬆是生活感受，不是治療聲稱。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不一定完全不知原因，也不能因效果好就略過必要努力或查核。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述具體正面效果，避免把比喻當作超自然或普遍保證。

sources.sentence: The quiet garden works its magic after a stressful day.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 3, table 1, row 4; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: After a busy afternoon, the quiet courtyard worked its magic: I slowed down and enjoyed a few peaceful minutes among the plants.
listening.zh: 忙碌下午後，安靜庭院發揮了迷人效果：我放慢下來，在植物間享受幾分鐘平靜。

options.en: It made the speaker rush to finish more tasks.
options.zh: 它令說話者趕着完成更多工作。

options.en: It helped the speaker slow down and enjoy a quiet pause.
options.zh: 它讓說話者放慢並享受安靜片刻。

options.en: The speaker already felt calm before entering, so the courtyard brought no change.
options.zh: 進去前說話者已感平靜，所以庭院沒有帶來改變。

options.en: It persuaded the speaker that everyone would react in the same way.
options.zh: 它讓說話者相信每個人都會有相同反應。

listening.explanationZh: slowed down 與 peaceful minutes 說明進入庭院後放慢的個人效果，不是進入前已平靜而毫無改變，也不保證人人同樣反應。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼你覺得那個庭院適合忙碌後坐一會？
reply.promptEn: Why did you like sitting in that courtyard after a busy afternoon?

options.en: Its quiet setting helped me slow down.
options.zh: 安靜環境幫我放慢。

options.en: The plants and quiet gave me a pleasant pause.
options.zh: 植物與寧靜讓我有愉快歇息。

options.en: It worked its magic and left me feeling calmer.
options.zh: 它發揮了迷人效果，讓我感覺更平靜。

options.en: I enjoyed sitting there without the afternoon rush.
options.zh: 我享受坐在那裏，暫離下午的忙亂。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都談具體個人感受；金句用 magic 的非字面說法。

scene.promptZh: 你看手藝人整理舊布料，熟練配搭後成為漂亮布袋，讚歎成果。哪句可自然表達？

options.en: Her careful design worked its magic on the old fabric.
options.zh: 她用心的設計在舊布料上發揮了迷人效果。

options.en: The design left the fabric unchanged, with no bag being made.
options.zh: 設計讓布料原封不動，沒有做成布袋。

options.en: The finished design made the old fabric less appealing to the observer.
options.zh: 完成的設計讓觀察者覺得舊布料較不吸引。

scene.explanationZh: 題目欣賞熟練配搭的悅人效果，可用 worked its magic；不是未有改變或覺得更不吸引。

contrast.promptZh: 哪句把 work its magic 理解得過頭？

options.en: It can praise a noticeable positive effect.
options.zh: 它可讚賞明顯正面效果。

options.en: It may describe a setting or a person’s skilled work.
options.zh: 它可描述環境或人的熟練工作。

options.en: It establishes that the same effect will occur for every person without exception.
options.zh: 它證明每個人毫無例外都會有相同效果。

contrast.explanationZh: 讚賞效果不等於普遍保證；要看具體人與情況。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「音樂 worked its magic，所以所有人都會立刻喜歡這場景」。哪句澄清最好？

options.en: It created a lovely effect for us, but other viewers may respond differently.
options.zh: 它對我們產生美好效果，但其他觀眾可能反應不同。

options.en: A different response from another viewer would make our own positive experience false.
options.zh: 另一位觀眾反應不同，會令我們自己的正面體驗變成虛假。

options.en: Our response is enough to establish how the other viewers felt.
options.zh: 我們的反應已足以確定其他觀眾感受。

dialogue.explanationZh: 個人讚賞不代表已知全體反應。

speaking.en: The soft music worked its magic as the room grew quieter.
speaking.zh: 房間漸漸安靜時，柔和音樂發揮了迷人效果。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再讚賞具體而非超自然的效果。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：聚會開始時陌生客人較拘謹，主持人用溫和幽默講小故事，漸漸有人開始聊天。用一至兩句英文讚賞這次具體效果，不保證對每個人都有效。

examples.en: The host’s gentle humour worked its magic, and guests began talking after an awkward start.
examples.zh: 主持人溫和幽默發揮了迷人效果，客人在拘謹開場後開始交談。

examples.en: Her friendly storytelling worked its magic on the gathering, making the conversation feel easier for the guests we observed.
examples.zh: 她友善的說故事方式在聚會發揮迷人效果，讓我們觀察到的客人較自然交談。

writing.selfCheckZh: 用這次觀察到的交談變化描述正面效果，不聲稱超自然或所有場合都相同。

takeaways.en: The garden works its magic on a quiet afternoon.
takeaways.zh: 安靜下午裏，花園發揮它迷人的效果。

takeaways.en: A skilled storyteller can work their magic without using elaborate props.
takeaways.zh: 熟練說故事的人不需複雜道具，也能發揮迷人效果。

brief.meaningEn: The most valued, impressive or admired part of a collection, organisation or place.
brief.meaningZh: 一組事物、機構或地方中最受珍視、最出色或最受讚賞的部分。
brief.grammar: the crown jewel of/in a collection; a metaphor from royal jewels.
brief.register: Strong approving expression; a judgement of relative value.
brief.boundaryZh: 不必是真珠寶或有皇室關係，也不一定最昂貴、最大或最古老；需交代在哪一組中最受重視。
brief.misconceptionZh: 有人稱某物為瑰寶，是價值判斷，不自動證明每人同意或已完成保育。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用具體受重視的特色支持相對地位，不把大小或價錢當唯一定義。

sources.sentence: The old theatre is the crown jewel of the district.

listening.en: The tiny reading room is the crown jewel of the restored station for local families, who value its rare books and welcoming volunteers.
listening.zh: 對本地家庭來說，小閱讀室是修復車站中最珍貴的瑰寶，因為他們重視珍本與親切義工。
listening.promptZh: 閱讀室為甚麼被稱為 crown jewel？

options.en: It has been judged the largest room by floor area.
options.zh: 它按面積被判定為最大房間。

options.en: Families particularly value its books and welcoming people.
options.zh: 家庭特別珍視它的書與親切服務者。

options.en: Its royal ownership is the only reason anyone visits.
options.zh: 皇室擁有權是人們到訪的唯一原因。

options.en: It is the only part of the station that has not been restored.
options.zh: 它是車站唯一未修復的部分。

listening.explanationZh: 題目以珍本及義工說明受重視，不是比較面積或皇室擁有。

reply.promptZh: 本地家庭為甚麼特別重視車站的閱讀室？
reply.promptEn: Why do local families value the station’s reading room so highly?

options.en: Its rare books and welcoming volunteers make it special.
options.zh: 珍本與親切義工讓它特別。

options.en: It is the crown jewel because of its rare books and welcoming volunteers.
options.zh: 它因珍本與親切義工而成為最珍貴的瑰寶。

options.en: They value its collection and the friendly place it provides.
options.zh: 他們重視館藏與它提供的友善地方。

options.en: Its rare collection and friendly help make it the station’s most treasured feature.
options.zh: 珍貴館藏及友善協助，讓它成為車站最受珍視的特色。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都說明特別價值；金句不是實際珠寶。

scene.promptZh: 小博物館的手稿不是最大展品，卻因獨特記錄及本地意義而最受珍視。哪句貼切？

options.en: Its size alone makes the manuscript the most important exhibit.
options.zh: 單憑大小，手稿就成為最重要展品。

options.en: The manuscript is the crown jewel of the collection.
options.zh: 手稿是館藏中最珍貴的瑰寶。

options.en: The manuscript is valued only because it cost more to acquire than the other items.
options.zh: 手稿只因購入成本高於其他物品才受珍視。

scene.explanationZh: 獨特記錄及本地意義支持珍視，不以尺寸或未交代的購入成本作根據。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論最不宜由 crown jewel 得出？

options.en: The speaker regards it as a particularly valued part of a group.
options.zh: 說話者視它為一組中尤其受重視的部分。

options.en: Its importance may come from cultural meaning rather than size.
options.zh: 重要性可來自文化意義而非大小。

options.en: It must have the highest price in an audited sales list.
options.zh: 它必須在經審核售價表中售價最高。

contrast.explanationZh: 瑰寶比喻價值與讚賞，不等於已完成價格排名。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「閱讀室很小，所以不能是 crown jewel」。哪句澄清最好？

options.en: A small feature can be the most treasured one because of what it offers.
options.zh: 小設施可以因提供的東西而最受珍視。

options.en: Let us use floor area as the only test of value.
options.zh: 只用面積衡量價值吧。

options.en: Only the most expensive feature can hold that title, so we should compare purchase prices.
options.zh: 只有最昂貴部分才配這稱呼，所以應比較購入價格。

dialogue.explanationZh: 相對珍視可以源於獨特內容，無需佔最大面積。

speaking.en: The old reading room is the crown jewel of the restored station.
speaking.zh: 舊閱讀室是修復車站中最珍貴的瑰寶。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再表達某組中最珍視的特色。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：青年計劃中，導師配對活動規模不最大，卻因個別回饋而最受學員珍視，大家視它為計劃最出色部分。用一至兩句英文說明價值。

examples.en: The mentoring scheme is the crown jewel of the youth programme because learners value its individual feedback.
examples.zh: 導師配對是青年計劃中最受珍視的瑰寶，因為學員重視個別回饋。

examples.en: Although larger events attract more people, the mentoring scheme remains the crown jewel of the programme for those who value personal guidance.
examples.zh: 雖然較大型活動吸引更多人，對重視個別指導的人而言，導師配對仍是計劃最珍貴的瑰寶。

writing.selfCheckZh: 把珍視連結到回饋價值，不以參加人數或經費大小作唯一定義。

takeaways.en: The theatre is the crown jewel of the district’s cultural buildings.
takeaways.zh: 劇院是該區文化建築中最受珍視的瑰寶。

takeaways.en: A small manuscript can be the crown jewel of a large collection.
takeaways.zh: 小手稿可以是大型館藏中最珍貴的瑰寶。

brief.meaningEn: Cause people to meet, cooperate or unite, or combine ideas or things in one setting.
brief.meaningZh: 讓人相聚、合作或團結，或把想法與事物放在一起結合。
brief.grammar: bring together + people/ideas; bring people/them together; past brought.
brief.register: Common phrasal verb; exact sense depends on the object.
brief.boundaryZh: 相聚可促進了解，不保證已同意或達成持久團結；結合想法也不等於把差別抹去。
brief.misconceptionZh: 同場相遇不是已解決分歧；要看有沒有討論及後續合作。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述活動讓原本分散的人相聚，並區分相聚與已同意。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: The festival can bring together neighbours from different streets.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 3, table 2, row 3; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: The repair workshop brought together neighbours who had never met before, giving them a chance to share tools and learn from one another.
listening.zh: 維修工作坊讓從未見面的鄰居相聚，給他們機會分享工具並互相學習。

options.en: Neighbours met and had an opportunity to share and learn.
options.zh: 鄰居相遇，並有機會分享與學習。

options.en: All neighbours had already become close friends before the event.
options.zh: 所有鄰居活動前已成為好友。

options.en: The organiser separated the neighbours so they could not exchange ideas.
options.zh: 主辦者把鄰居分隔，讓他們不能交流想法。

options.en: The event settled every future disagreement about shared tools.
options.zh: 活動解決了日後有關共用工具的所有分歧。

listening.explanationZh: never met before 與 chance 顯示建立相遇機會，不保證全部未來結果。

reply.promptZh: 維修工作坊給街坊帶來甚麼機會？
reply.promptEn: What opportunity did the repair workshop give local residents?

options.en: It allowed neighbours who had not met before to meet.
options.zh: 它讓原未見面的鄰居相遇。

options.en: It brought people together to share tools and skills.
options.zh: 它讓人相聚，分享工具與技能。

options.en: It created a place for people to learn from one another.
options.zh: 它創造讓人互相學習的地方。

options.en: People who had not met could exchange practical ideas.
options.zh: 原未見面的人可以交流實用想法。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都說明相遇與交流機會；金句用 bring people together。

scene.promptZh: 學校邀不同社團同場討論可共享的資源，大家首次互相認識，但仍在比較建議。哪句準確？

options.en: The meeting brought people together without yet settling every proposal.
options.zh: 會議讓人相聚，但仍未議定每項提案。

options.en: The meeting confirmed that the clubs had already agreed all resource rules.
options.zh: 會議確認社團已同意所有資源規則。

options.en: The meeting prevented clubs from meeting or hearing one another.
options.zh: 會議阻止社團相遇或互聽意見。

scene.explanationZh: 首次認識支持相聚；仍比較建議不支持全部規則已定。

contrast.promptZh: 哪句把 bring people together 的含意說得過頭？

options.en: The activity enables people to meet or cooperate.
options.zh: 活動讓人相遇或合作。

options.en: People can be brought together while still holding different views.
options.zh: 人們相聚後仍可有不同看法。

options.en: Their meeting proves that all disagreements have been resolved.
options.zh: 他們相遇證明所有分歧已解決。

contrast.explanationZh: 接觸及合作機會不等於全部分歧消失。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「論壇 brought people together，所以不用再聽不同意見」。哪句回應最好？

options.en: Let us use attendance as approval of the final proposal.
options.zh: 把出席當作批准最後提案吧。

options.en: Meeting creates a chance to talk; we still need to hear and discuss the differences.
options.zh: 相遇創造交談機會；我們仍需聽取及討論差異。

options.en: Once people share a room, further discussion of their differences is unnecessary.
options.zh: 人們一旦在同一房間，就不需再討論差異。

dialogue.explanationZh: 聚集是交流的開端，不是已有共識的證據。

speaking.en: The workshop brought people together to share practical skills.
speaking.zh: 工作坊讓人相聚，分享實用技能。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明活動如何促成交流。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你們製作無障礙參觀小冊，把路線測量、訪客意見及現場草圖放入同一指南，保留不同資料的用途。用一至兩句英文描述整合。

examples.en: The guide brings together route measurements, visitor comments and sketches so readers can compare the different kinds of information.
examples.zh: 指南匯合路線測量、訪客意見及草圖，讓讀者比較不同資料。

examples.en: By bringing together measurements and personal accounts, the booklet offers a fuller view without treating those sources as identical.
examples.zh: 小冊把測量與個人敘述結合，提供較完整看法，而不把來源當作相同。

writing.selfCheckZh: 這次匯合的是資料而非人群；說明放在一起的用途，保留測量及個人意見的差異。

takeaways.en: A shared project can bring people together.
takeaways.zh: 共同項目可以讓人相聚。

takeaways.en: The exhibition brought together ideas from several different communities.
takeaways.zh: 展覽匯合了幾個不同社區的想法。

chinese.evidence: Traditional Chinese translations checked against each English sentence; not independent human approval.

titleZh: 讓地方變得熱鬧有活力

target.pattern: \b(?:bring|brings|bringing|brought) (?:a whole street|the street|the square|the courtyard|the school|a place|it) to life\b

brief.meaningEn: Make a place feel lively, active and full of people or activity.
brief.meaningZh: 令地方充滿活動與人流，顯得熱鬧而有活力。
brief.grammar: bring a street/square/place to life; past brought; lively-place sense in this lesson.
brief.register: Common life metaphor applied to places.
brief.boundaryZh: 不表示街道成為生物，也不必永久改變；與把故事或藝術呈現得生動的另一用法相關，但本課看地方的實際活動。
brief.misconceptionZh: 一晚熱鬧不足以證明全年改善或所有居民都喜歡；要保留時段與證據。
brief.outcomeZh: 能以攤檔、人流及交流描述地方短期活力，不推及未查證的長期效果。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.expression: bring a whole street to life
sources.sentence: A night market can bring a whole street to life.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 3, table 2, row 4; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: For one evening, the outdoor reading event brought the courtyard to life, with neighbours talking, browsing books and listening to stories.
listening.zh: 那一晚，戶外閱讀活動讓庭院活起來，鄰居交談、翻閱書籍並聽故事。

options.en: It made the space active with people and shared activities that evening.
options.zh: 它讓那晚的空間充滿人流及共同活動。

options.en: It proved the courtyard would stay equally busy throughout the year.
options.zh: 它證明庭院全年都會一樣忙。

options.en: It left the courtyard unused because the event moved elsewhere.
options.zh: 活動移往別處，令庭院無人使用。

options.en: It mainly produced a more vivid illustration of a courtyard in a book.
options.zh: 它主要把書中庭院插畫呈現得更生動。

listening.explanationZh: 實際鄰里活動令地方熱鬧；for one evening 限定時段，不是藝術呈現或全年保證。

reply.promptZh: 那晚閱讀活動對庭院氣氛有甚麼影響？
reply.promptEn: How did the reading event affect the courtyard’s atmosphere that evening?

options.en: Neighbours filled it with conversations and stories.
options.zh: 鄰居讓它充滿交談與故事。

options.en: It brought the courtyard to life.
options.zh: 它讓庭院變得熱鬧有活力。

options.en: The normally quiet space became busy and welcoming.
options.zh: 平常安靜的空間變得熱鬧親切。

options.en: People browsing and listening gave the space a lively atmosphere.
options.zh: 翻書及聽故事的人讓空間充滿活力。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描述地方當晚的實際活力；金句用生命意象。

scene.promptZh: 一條平常少人的街道周末設小攤及表演，鄰里來往交流。你只觀察到這個周末。哪句最準確？

options.en: The event shows that every later weekend will have the same activity.
options.zh: 活動顯示之後每個周末都會有相同活動。

options.en: The event kept the street empty while attracting people to a different area.
options.zh: 活動吸引人去別區，同時讓街道空着。

options.en: The market brought the street to life that weekend.
options.zh: 市集在那個周末讓街道熱鬧起來。

scene.explanationZh: 攤檔、人流及交流支持當時活力，不足以斷定所有往後周末。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不像本課 bring a place to life？

options.en: A square fills with people exchanging food and stories.
options.zh: 廣場滿是交換食物與故事的人。

options.en: A courtyard stays unused and silent while the planned event is cancelled.
options.zh: 計劃活動取消，庭院維持無人使用且安靜。

options.en: Small stalls make a formerly quiet street feel active for the evening.
options.zh: 小攤讓原本安靜的街道那晚顯得有活力。

contrast.explanationZh: 本課需實際活動帶來地方活力，不是活動取消後仍空着。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「市集 brought the street to life，所以不用再問居民對長期安排的意見」。哪句回應最好？

options.en: The evening was lively; a long-term plan still needs residents’ views.
options.zh: 那晚很熱鬧；長期計劃仍需居民意見。

options.en: Let us treat the crowd as support for the same schedule every night.
options.zh: 把人潮當作支持每晚相同安排吧。

options.en: The lively atmosphere is enough evidence that no further consultation is needed.
options.zh: 熱鬧氣氛已足以證明不需進一步諮詢。

dialogue.explanationZh: 短期活力不等於長期時間表或居民意見已確定。

speaking.en: The small market brought the square to life for the evening.
speaking.zh: 小市集讓廣場在那晚熱鬧起來。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再以具體時段描述地方活力。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：假期後學生重回學校，走廊再有腳步、招呼及活動，原本安靜的校舍在上學早上恢復活力。用一至兩句英文描述當時氣氛，不推論全年每天都相同。

examples.en: The students’ return brought the school to life after the holiday, filling the corridors with footsteps and greetings.
examples.zh: 假期後學生回來，腳步與招呼聲充滿走廊，讓學校恢復活力。

examples.en: On the first morning back, ordinary conversations and activity brought the school to life again.
examples.zh: 返校第一個早上，平常交談與活動讓學校重新活起來。

writing.selfCheckZh: 用學生回來後的腳步、招呼及平常活動描述地方活力，保留返校第一個早上的時段，不推成全年相同。

takeaways.en: The evening festival brought the street to life.
takeaways.zh: 晚間節慶讓街道熱鬧起來。

takeaways.en: A regular gathering can bring a place to life without changing its buildings.
takeaways.zh: 固定聚會可以不改建築，也讓地方充滿活力。

titleZh: 透過當下活動傳承歷史

brief.meaningEn: A place or practice that keeps history visible through continuing activity, demonstration or participation.
brief.meaningZh: 透過持續活動、示範或參與，讓歷史仍可被看見的地方或做法。
brief.grammar: a living museum of + tradition/craft/history; plural living museums.
brief.register: Figurative cultural description in this lesson; not a guarantee of official museum status.
brief.boundaryZh: 不只把舊物放櫃內，而是當下仍展示或實踐傳統；稱呼不代表技法永遠原封不動，也不排除新工具。
brief.misconceptionZh: 有人仍在活動不表示每項細節都與過去相同；歷史呈現與完全不變不同。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用現場示範與持續實踐支持傳承歷史的比喻。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: The workshops are living museums of local craftsmanship.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 3, table 2, row 5; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: The weaving workshop is a living museum of local craft: makers demonstrate old patterns while younger learners practise beside them.
listening.zh: 織布工作坊像本地工藝的活博物館：師傅示範舊圖案，年輕學員在旁練習。
listening.promptZh: 甚麼讓工作坊像 living museum？

options.en: Old tools are locked away with no demonstration or use.
options.zh: 舊工具被鎖起，沒有示範或使用。

options.en: The craft is practised and passed on through current activity.
options.zh: 工藝透過當下活動被實踐及傳授。

options.en: Only a future proposal exists; no makers or learners are present.
options.zh: 只有未來提案，沒有師傅或學員在場。

options.en: The workshop presents history through display labels alone, with no live teaching.
options.zh: 工作坊只透過展品標籤呈現歷史，沒有現場教學。

listening.explanationZh: 示範及學員實踐讓歷史活在當下，不只是靜態收藏。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼你說織布工作坊能讓人看到活着的工藝歷史？
reply.promptEn: Why do you say the weaving workshop shows craft history in a living way?

options.en: Makers demonstrate inherited patterns while students practise them.
options.zh: 師傅示範傳下的圖案，學生同時練習。

options.en: It is a living museum because people still demonstrate and teach weaving there.
options.zh: 它是活博物館，因為人們仍在那裏示範及教授織布。

options.en: Visitors see the tradition being used and taught today.
options.zh: 訪客看見傳統今天仍被運用及教授。

options.en: The skills remain visible through hands-on learning.
options.zh: 技能透過親手學習仍清楚可見。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以當下示範與學習解釋傳承；金句用博物館比喻。

scene.promptZh: 老店仍以傳承方法製作糕點，師傅一邊工作一邊教徒弟，訪客可看過程。哪句有根據？

options.en: The shop is a living museum of a continuing food tradition.
options.zh: 老店是持續飲食傳統的活博物館。

options.en: The shop preserves only unused tools while no one practises the craft.
options.zh: 老店只保留未用工具，無人實踐工藝。

options.en: The shop has stopped making food and now shows only future design plans.
options.zh: 老店已停止做食品，現在只展示未來設計計劃。

scene.explanationZh: 正在製作及教學讓歷史透過活動可見。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項資料最不足以單獨支持本課的 living museum？

options.en: People demonstrate a traditional skill for visitors.
options.zh: 人們向訪客示範傳統技能。

options.en: Learners practise a craft alongside experienced makers.
options.zh: 學員在有經驗師傅旁練習工藝。

options.en: A label lists old objects, but no continuing practice or demonstration is described.
options.zh: 標籤列出舊物，但未描述持續實踐或示範。

contrast.explanationZh: 本課重點是當下持續實踐，只有舊物清單不足以支持。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「living museum 意味着師傅不能調整任何工具」。哪句澄清最好？

options.en: Let us judge tradition only by whether every tool is identical to the oldest example.
options.zh: 只按每件工具是否與最古老例子完全相同判斷傳統吧。

options.en: It highlights history through continuing practice, not a rule that every detail must stay unchanged.
options.zh: 它強調透過持續實踐呈現歷史，不是規定每個細節不能改變。

options.en: Updating one tool means the continuing teaching no longer counts as heritage.
options.zh: 更新一件工具，表示持續教學也不再算傳承。

dialogue.explanationZh: 傳承可有延續及調整，不由比喻推出所有工具永遠不變。

speaking.en: The workshop is a living museum where older skills are still taught and practised.
speaking.zh: 工作坊是活博物館，舊技能仍在這裏被教授及實踐。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明歷史如何透過當下活動延續。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：一座保留舊鐵路工藝的車站仍讓師傅示範操作及教年輕人，但訪客資訊改用電子時間表。你想說歷史仍透過活動延續，不必每項工具不變。用一至兩句英文描述。

examples.en: The station is a living museum of railway skills, with demonstrations and teaching continuing alongside an electronic visitor timetable.
examples.zh: 車站是鐵路技能的活博物館，示範及教學持續，同時也有電子訪客時間表。

examples.en: Using a modern timetable does not stop the station being a living museum; older skills remain visible through the work people still demonstrate.
examples.zh: 用現代時間表不妨礙車站成為活博物館；人們仍示範的工作讓舊技能可見。

writing.selfCheckZh: 同時交代持續示範及更新資訊工具，不把活態傳承誤成每個細節必須不變。

takeaways.en: The working mill is a living museum of local skills.
takeaways.zh: 仍運作的磨坊是本地技能的活博物館。

takeaways.en: Living museums make history visible through present activity.
takeaways.zh: 活博物館透過當下活動讓歷史可見。

listening.en: Family recipes carry culture across generations when people share the food, the stories behind it and the occasions when it is prepared.
listening.zh: 家傳食譜在分享食物、背後故事及製作場合時，跨世代承載文化。

options.en: Only the shopping price is passed on, with no shared meaning.
options.zh: 只傳下購買價格，沒有共同意義。

options.en: The recipe replaces every other source of cultural identity.
options.zh: 食譜取代所有其他文化身份來源。

options.en: Food is linked with shared stories and occasions across generations.
options.zh: 食物跨世代連結共同故事與場合。

options.en: The account proves that every family prepares it in exactly the same way.
options.zh: 敘述證明每個家庭製法完全相同。

listening.explanationZh: 故事及場合說明共同意義的傳遞，不只價格，也不聲稱全體一樣。

reply.promptZh: 家傳食譜為甚麼不只是配料清單？
reply.promptEn: Why is a family recipe more than a list of ingredients?

options.en: It connects the food with family stories and occasions.
options.zh: 它把食物連結到家族故事與場合。

options.en: It can carry culture from one generation to another.
options.zh: 它可以把文化從一代傳到另一代。

options.en: Preparing it can pass on shared meanings as well as cooking methods.
options.zh: 製作它可傳遞共同意義及烹調方法。

options.en: It helps younger relatives learn why the dish matters to the family.
options.zh: 它幫年幼親人了解菜式對家庭的重要性。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都說明食物以外的文化連結；金句用承載比喻。

scene.promptZh: 長者教孩子唱一首節日歌曲，同時解釋歌詞故事及聚會習俗。哪句準確？

options.en: The song carries culture through its words, stories and shared use.
options.zh: 歌曲透過歌詞、故事及共同運用承載文化。

options.en: The lesson passes on melody alone while avoiding the words and customs.
options.zh: 課堂只傳旋律，避談歌詞與習俗。

options.en: The song is presented only as solo entertainment, without a connection to shared festival customs.
options.zh: 歌曲只作獨唱娛樂呈現，未連結共同節日習俗。

scene.explanationZh: 故事、歌詞及共同節日習俗提供文化傳遞，不是只學旋律或孤立娛樂。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論最不宜由一首歌 carries culture 得出？

options.en: The song can express meanings valued by a community.
options.zh: 歌曲可以表達社群重視的意義。

options.en: The song represents every member’s experience in exactly the same way.
options.zh: 歌曲以完全相同方式代表每位成員的經歷。

options.en: Teaching its story can help pass meanings to younger people.
options.zh: 教授它的故事可幫助向年輕人傳遞意義。

contrast.explanationZh: 文化可共享且多樣，不等於每位成員經驗相同。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「食譜改了少許，就不可能 carry culture」。哪句回應最好？

options.en: Let us judge its cultural role only by whether ingredient quantities have ever changed.
options.zh: 只按配料份量是否曾改變判斷文化角色吧。

options.en: Only the ingredient list carries cultural meaning, so the family stories are irrelevant.
options.zh: 只有配料清單承載文化意義，所以家族故事不相關。

options.en: A recipe can change while still passing on family stories and shared meanings.
options.zh: 食譜可以改變，同時仍傳遞家族故事與共同意義。

dialogue.explanationZh: 形式可以調整，仍須看意義與習俗有沒有延續。

speaking.en: Family stories carry culture across generations.
speaking.zh: 家族故事跨世代承載文化。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再描述共同意義如何被傳下去。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：外地社區透過節日舞蹈分享原鄉故事，因場地較小稍改動步法，但仍解釋共同意義。用一至兩句英文說明文化傳遞可以伴隨形式調整。

examples.en: The festival dance carries culture through its stories and shared meanings, even when the steps are adapted for a smaller stage.
examples.zh: 節日舞蹈透過故事與共同意義承載文化，即使步法因較小舞台而調整。

examples.en: By explaining the story while performing adapted steps, the community carries culture without keeping every movement unchanged.
examples.zh: 社群表演調整過的步法時也解釋故事，讓文化傳下去，不必每個動作都原封不動。

writing.selfCheckZh: 指出故事與意義仍在傳遞，同時保留場地帶來形式調整，不把改動當作完全失去文化。

takeaways.en: Songs can carry culture as well as entertain listeners.
takeaways.zh: 歌曲可以承載文化，也娛樂聽眾。

takeaways.en: Recipes may carry culture even as families adapt ingredients over time.
takeaways.zh: 家庭隨時間調整配料時，食譜仍可能承載文化。

listening.en: The small rehearsal rooms form part of the district’s cultural heartbeat, with local groups returning each week to make music and share ideas.
listening.zh: 小排練室是該區文化脈動的一部分，本地團體每周回來做音樂並交流想法。
listening.promptZh: 排練室為甚麼有這個文化角色？

options.en: They provide space for regular local creativity and exchange.
options.zh: 它們為定期本地創作及交流提供空間。

options.en: Their importance comes only from a one-off opening ceremony.
options.zh: 它們的重要性只來自一次開幕禮。

options.en: They show that the district’s cultural activity has stopped.
options.zh: 它們顯示該區文化活動已停止。

options.en: The rooms are used only to store instruments, not for regular practice or exchange.
options.zh: 房間只用來存樂器，而非定期練習或交流。

listening.explanationZh: 每周做音樂及交流，支持持續文化活力；不是只一次開幕、活動停止或房間只用來儲存樂器。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼小排練室對這區的文化生活重要？
reply.promptEn: Why do the small rehearsal rooms matter to the district’s cultural life?

options.en: Local groups return weekly to make music there.
options.zh: 本地團體每周回來做音樂。

options.en: Regular music and exchange make them part of the district’s cultural heartbeat.
options.zh: 定期音樂及交流，讓它們成為該區文化脈動的一部分。

options.en: They support regular creativity and exchanges among neighbours.
options.zh: 它們支持鄰里定期創作及交流。

options.en: They keep a place available for people to practise and develop ideas together.
options.zh: 它們保留地方讓人一起練習及發展想法。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描述持續活動的作用；金句用心跳比喻文化活力。

scene.promptZh: 小書店每周讀詩、讓新作者交流，附近居民多年參與，不只開幕當天熱鬧。哪句有支持？

options.en: Its role ended at the opening, with no later activity.
options.zh: 它的角色在開幕結束，之後沒有活動。

options.en: The bookshop is part of the neighbourhood’s cultural heartbeat.
options.zh: 書店是社區文化脈動的一部分。

options.en: The weekly sessions show that residents have stopped sharing creative work.
options.zh: 每周聚會顯示居民已停止分享創作。

scene.explanationZh: 多年反覆讀詩及交流支持持續活力。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項資料最不足以單獨支持持續 cultural heartbeat？

options.en: Regular workshops help residents practise and share creative work.
options.zh: 定期工作坊幫居民練習及分享創作。

options.en: A small venue hosts ongoing performances and discussions.
options.zh: 小場地持續舉辦演出與討論。

options.en: A venue has an impressive opening photograph, but no later cultural activity is described.
options.zh: 場地有精彩開幕照片，但沒有描述之後文化活動。

contrast.explanationZh: 持續文化活力需有後續活動證據，不只一次照片。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「只有大型節慶才算 cultural heartbeat」。哪句回應最好？

options.en: Small, regular creative gatherings can sustain cultural energy too.
options.zh: 小型、定期創作聚會也能維持文化活力。

options.en: Let us measure cultural life only by the size of the annual crowd.
options.zh: 只按年度人潮大小衡量文化生活吧。

options.en: Weekly local groups should be left out of the account because their venues are small.
options.zh: 因場地小，應把每周本地團體活動排除在描述外。

dialogue.explanationZh: 比喻指持續活力與身份，不把規模當唯一標準。

speaking.en: The weekly gatherings are part of the neighbourhood’s cultural heartbeat.
speaking.zh: 每周聚會是社區文化脈動的一部分。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再以心跳意象描述持續文化活動。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：街坊在不同家中錄製每月社區聲音節目，分享新詩、舊故事及音樂，持續多年，沒有固定大場館。用一至兩句英文描述這種分散創作的文化作用。

examples.en: The monthly neighbourhood programme is part of the area’s cultural heartbeat, sharing new poems, older stories and music from people’s homes.
examples.zh: 每月街坊節目是地區文化脈動的一部分，從人們家中分享新詩、舊故事及音樂。

examples.en: Regular recordings keep the community’s cultural heartbeat going, even without a large venue, because local people continue creating and sharing.
examples.zh: 即使沒有大場館，定期錄音仍讓社群文化脈動持續，因為本地人繼續創作及分享。

writing.selfCheckZh: 用每月及持續多年創作支持活力，不把固定場館或一場大型活動當必要條件。

takeaways.en: Small venues can sustain a city’s cultural heartbeat.
takeaways.zh: 小場地可以維持城市文化脈動。

takeaways.en: The cultural heartbeat of a neighbourhood includes quiet, regular creativity as well as festivals.
takeaways.zh: 社區文化脈動包括安靜、定期的創作，也包括節慶。

titleZh: 實際情況涉及更多因素

brief.meaningEn: The overall situation includes more factors, groups or possibilities than the initial view suggested.
brief.meaningZh: 整體情況比最初看法涉及更多因素、群體或可能性。
brief.grammar: the picture is (much) broader once/when we include + factor; broader is comparative, much intensifies.
brief.register: Conventional picture metaphor for the overall situation.
brief.boundaryZh: 不是畫框尺寸改大；擴大考慮範圍不自動等於較好、較差或改動每項原結論。
brief.misconceptionZh: 加入重要因素應修正解釋，但不能因此忽略原有相關證據；broader 比較考慮範圍。
brief.outcomeZh: 能說明最初遺漏甚麼，並把新因素加入整體判斷。

listening.en: At first we counted only full-time staff, but the picture is broader when we include volunteers and part-time helpers who also keep the service running.
listening.zh: 起初我們只計全職員工，但把同樣維持服務的義工及兼職幫手包括在內，整體情況就涉及更多人。
listening.promptZh: 說話者怎樣擴大考慮範圍？

options.en: By replacing information about all workers with the full-time count alone.
options.zh: 以單計全職人數，取代所有工作者資訊。

options.en: By including other people who contribute to the service.
options.zh: 把其他為服務作貢獻的人包括在內。

options.en: By showing that full-time staff never contributed to the service.
options.zh: 顯示全職員工從未為服務作貢獻。

options.en: By concluding the service must be worse because more groups are involved.
options.zh: 因更多群體參與而斷定服務必定更差。

listening.explanationZh: 包括義工及兼職使範圍更廣，不是否認全職貢獻或自動評價好壞。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼單計全職員工不足以了解服務如何運作？
reply.promptEn: Why is counting only full-time staff insufficient to understand how the service runs?

options.en: Volunteers and part-time helpers also contribute.
options.zh: 義工及兼職幫手也有貢獻。

options.en: The first count leaves out some people who keep it running.
options.zh: 最初計算漏掉部分維持服務的人。

options.en: The picture is broader when we include everyone who helps.
options.zh: 把所有幫忙的人包括在內，整體情況涉及更多人。

options.en: We need to consider other kinds of support as well as full-time work.
options.zh: 除全職工作外，我們需考慮其他支援。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都指出遺漏的貢獻者；金句用 picture 描述整體情況。

scene.promptZh: 你初時只看巴士車程判斷上學時間，後來加入步行、等車及轉車。哪句準確？

options.en: The picture is broader once walking and waiting are included.
options.zh: 加入步行及等車後，整體情況涉及更多因素。

options.en: The added factors show that time spent on the bus no longer matters at all.
options.zh: 新增因素顯示巴士上的時間已完全不重要。

options.en: Including the extra stages by itself proves every route takes the same time.
options.zh: 加入額外階段本身就證明每條路線需時相同。

scene.explanationZh: 新因素擴大估算範圍，不取消巴士時間或證明路線相同。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個理解最不符合 the picture is broader？

options.en: The first account omitted a relevant group or factor.

options.en: More than the initially considered issue is involved.
options.zh: 所涉及的不只最初考慮的問題。

options.en: The description concerns only a physically wider photograph, with no change in understanding the situation.
options.zh: 描述只關乎實際較寬照片，對情況理解沒有改變。

contrast.explanationZh: 本課 picture 是整體情況的比喻，broader 指考慮範圍。

options.en: Let us replace travel evidence with family needs rather than consider both.
options.zh: 以家庭需要取代交通證據，不同時考慮兩者吧。

options.en: The new factor widens our view; the relevant transport evidence still belongs in the assessment.
options.zh: 新因素擴大看法；相關交通證據仍應保留在評估中。

options.en: A broader view means keeping only the factor added most recently.
options.zh: 較廣看法表示只保留最近加入的因素。

dialogue.explanationZh: 擴大範圍是把相關因素結合，不只換成最新因素。

speaking.en: The picture is broader when we include the people who work behind the scenes.
speaking.zh: 把幕後工作的人包括在內，整體情況涉及更多人。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明原本遺漏的因素。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你們研究一條舊街，最初只讀官方文件，後來加入長期居民口述及家庭照片，發現更多生活細節。用一至兩句英文說明理解範圍擴大，仍保留原文件。

examples.en: The picture is broader when residents’ accounts and family photographs are considered alongside the official records.
examples.zh: 把居民敘述及家庭照片與官方紀錄一併考慮，整體情況涉及更多面向。

examples.en: Official records remain useful, but the picture is much broader once we include everyday experiences recalled by long-term residents.
examples.zh: 官方紀錄仍有用，但加入長期居民回憶的日常經驗後，整體情況廣泛得多。

writing.selfCheckZh: 用不同來源新增生活面向支持更廣理解，不把新口述當作須刪掉官方資料的理由。

takeaways.en: The picture is broader when we consider smaller organisations too.
takeaways.zh: 同時考慮小機構，整體情況涉及更多群體。

takeaways.en: The picture is much broader once we include family needs as well as work demands.
takeaways.zh: 同時包括家庭需要及工作要求，整體情況涉及的因素多得多。
