options.zh: 它刪除全部數碼版本，只展示紙本畫。

options.en: It established that every portrait in other exhibitions had already become digital.
options.zh: 它確定其他展覽的每幅肖像已全變成數碼。

listening.explanationZh: digital versions on monitors 是媒介變化；a few originals retained 保留實體部分與展覽範圍。

reply.promptZh: 這次肖像展的呈現方式有甚麼變化？
reply.promptEn: How did the presentation of portraits change in this exhibition?

options.en: Digital versions appeared on monitors alongside a few originals.
options.zh: 數碼版本出現在顯示器，旁邊仍有幾幅原作。

options.en: The portraits moved from the frame to the screen.
options.zh: 肖像從實體畫框走向螢幕呈現。

options.en: The artist used screen-based versions for much of the display.
options.zh: 藝術家在大部分展示使用螢幕版本。

options.en: The display shifted towards digital presentation without removing every drawing.
options.zh: 展示轉向數碼呈現，沒有移除每幅原稿。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描述特定展覽的媒介變化；金句用 frame/screen 作對比。

scene.promptZh: 小畫廊把部分紙本插畫製成投影及螢幕作品，仍保留原稿區。哪句準確？

options.en: For part of the display, the illustrations moved from the frame to the screen.
options.zh: 部分展示中，插畫從畫框走向螢幕。

options.en: The gallery kept every work on paper and introduced no screen-based versions.
options.zh: 畫廊把所有作品保留在紙上，沒有加入螢幕版本。

options.en: The display shows that physical originals have disappeared from every gallery.
options.zh: 展示顯示實體原稿已從每間畫廊消失。

scene.explanationZh: 部分改數碼、部分留原稿，需保留範圍，不推及所有畫廊。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項描述最不足以支持本課的 move from the frame to the screen？

options.en: An artist adapts framed drawings into digital versions on monitors.
options.zh: 藝術家把有框畫作改成顯示器上的數碼版本。

options.en: A display shifts towards projected images while keeping some originals.
options.zh: 展示轉向投影影像，同時保留部分原作。

options.en: A framed painting is moved beside an unused screen but remains the only displayed work.
options.zh: 有框畫被移到未用螢幕旁，卻仍是唯一展示作品。

contrast.explanationZh: 只有位置改動而沒有螢幕呈現，未支持媒介轉變。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「作品 moved from the frame to the screen，所以數碼版一定較好」。哪句回應最好？

options.en: The phrase describes a change of medium; we still need reasons to compare the experience.
options.zh: 片語描述媒介變化；比較體驗仍需理由。

options.en: Let us judge artistic quality from the presence of a monitor alone.
options.zh: 只按有沒有顯示器判斷藝術品質吧。

options.en: If any originals remain, we cannot describe even part of the display as moving to screens.
options.zh: 只要仍有原稿，就不能說展示有任何部分轉向螢幕。

dialogue.explanationZh: 媒介描述不提供品質排名，需看作品及觀賞體驗。

speaking.en: The display moved from the frame to the screen while keeping a small section of original drawings.
speaking.zh: 展示從畫框走向螢幕，同時保留一小區原稿。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再描述有範圍的媒介轉移。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：本地插畫員想讓外地社區也看到作品，計劃把原來掛在工作室的有框畫作製成線上螢幕版本，實體原稿仍保留。用一至兩句英文描述呈現及接觸方式改變，不判定品質一定提升。

examples.en: Her illustrations will move from the frame to the screen so an overseas community can view them online, while the originals stay in her studio.
examples.zh: 她的插畫將從畫框走向螢幕，讓外地社區可在線觀看，而原稿仍留在工作室。

examples.en: The presentation will move from the frame to the screen for viewers abroad, without replacing the physical drawings kept by the artist.
examples.zh: 呈現將為外地觀眾從畫框走向螢幕，同時不取代藝術家保存的實體畫作。

writing.selfCheckZh: 說明外地觀看目的及實際線上媒介，保留原稿存在，不由媒介直接推斷藝術品質。

takeaways.en: The exhibition moved from the frame to the screen for its digital section.
takeaways.zh: 展覽在數碼區從畫框走向螢幕。

takeaways.en: Art can move from the frame to the screen without making physical drawings obsolete.
takeaways.zh: 藝術可以從畫框走向螢幕，而不令實體畫作過時。

brief.meaningEn: Physically enter installation artworks designed to surround visitors with an experience.
brief.meaningZh: 親身走入裝置藝術之中，置身作品所營造的環境。
brief.grammar: walk into immersive installations; into marks movement from outside to inside.
brief.register: Natural literal description of visitor participation, not an idiom.
brief.boundaryZh: 沉浸可用光、聲、空間或材料，不一定數碼、觸控或戴頭盔；進入作品不等於可觸碰所有物件。
brief.misconceptionZh: 觀看照片與走入空間不同；進入許可也不自動等於全面互動許可。
brief.outcomeZh: 能區分實際進入裝置與只在外觀看，保留參與規則。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Visitors can walk into immersive installations at the new museum.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 4, table 1, row 4; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: At the new gallery, visitors can walk into immersive installations made of light and fabric, although signs ask them not to touch the hanging material.
listening.zh: 新畫廊讓訪客走進由光與布料構成的沉浸式裝置，但告示請他們不要觸碰垂掛材料。

options.en: They may enter the space but should follow the no-touch instruction.
options.zh: 他們可進入空間，但應遵守不觸碰指示。

options.en: They may view only photographs of the work from another room.
options.zh: 他們只可在另一房間看作品照片。

options.en: Entering the work means the no-touch signs do not apply.
options.zh: 進入作品表示不觸碰告示不適用。

options.en: They must wear a headset because every immersive work requires one.
options.zh: 他們必須戴頭盔，因為每件沉浸式作品都需要。

listening.explanationZh: 可走入與不可觸碰可同時成立；題目沒有頭盔要求。

reply.promptZh: 這畫廊與只在外面看作品的展覽有甚麼不同？
reply.promptEn: How is this gallery different from an exhibition viewed only from outside?

options.en: Visitors can enter the spaces formed by light and fabric.
options.zh: 訪客可進入光與布料構成的空間。

options.en: They can walk into immersive installations.
options.zh: 他們可走進沉浸式裝置。

options.en: People experience the artwork from within its environment.
options.zh: 人們從作品環境內體驗藝術。

options.en: The display lets people move inside rather than remain outside looking at it.
options.zh: 展示讓人走到內部，而非只在外觀看。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描述實際進入作品空間；金句不表示可任意觸碰。

scene.promptZh: 學生沿指定通道走入幾個光與聲音構成的房間，置身各作品中；旁邊也有只供外觀的展品。哪句描述這種參與？

options.en: They view only a flat photograph without entering the work.
options.zh: 他們只看平面照片，沒有進入作品。

options.en: They walk into immersive installations and experience the environment from inside.
options.zh: 他們走進沉浸式裝置，從內部體驗環境。

options.en: The room is closed to visitors, who can see it only in the catalogue.
options.zh: 房間不准訪客進入，他們只可在目錄看見。

scene.explanationZh: 指定通道及置身房間支持實際進入，不是照片觀看。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項許可最不能單憑 walk into immersive installations 就推斷？

options.en: Visitors may move from outside into the work’s space.
options.zh: 訪客可從外走進作品空間。

options.en: The experience can surround the visitor with light or sound.
options.zh: 體驗可用光或聲音包圍訪客。

options.en: Visitors may touch or move any component regardless of the gallery’s instructions.
options.zh: 不論畫廊指示，訪客可觸碰或移動任何組件。

contrast.explanationZh: 進入不同於任意觸碰；仍須遵守作品及場地規則。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「immersive 就一定要戴虛擬實境頭盔」。哪句澄清最好？

options.en: Immersion can come from a physical space of light, sound or materials without a headset.
options.zh: 光、聲或材料構成的實體空間，不用頭盔也可帶來沉浸感。

options.en: Seeing a photograph gives the same spatial experience as moving through the installation.
options.zh: 看照片與走過裝置空間的體驗相同。

options.en: Without a headset, the surrounding light and sound cannot create an immersive experience.
options.zh: 沒有頭盔，周圍光與聲音就不能帶來沉浸體驗。

dialogue.explanationZh: 沉浸是環境體驗，不限一種裝置或數碼技術。

speaking.en: Visitors can walk into immersive installations while following the marked route.
speaking.zh: 訪客可沿標示路線走進沉浸式裝置。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再描述親身走入作品的方式。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：設計節用巨大紙屋構成幾個可進入的裝置，訪客從內看窗戶與巷道，體驗跟只看外部照片不同。用一至兩句英文介紹空間參與，不自行假定可觸碰材料。

examples.en: Visitors can walk into immersive installations made of giant paper houses and see the imagined streets from inside.
examples.zh: 訪客可走進巨大紙屋構成的沉浸式裝置，從內部觀看想像街道。

examples.en: We walked into immersive installations at the design festival; experiencing the paper rooms from within was different from viewing a photograph.
examples.zh: 我們在設計節走進沉浸式裝置；從內部體驗紙房間，與看照片不同。

writing.selfCheckZh: 把實際進入後的空間視角與照片觀看比較，不把進入自動當作可觸碰或移動材料。

takeaways.en: We walked into immersive installations built around changing light.
takeaways.zh: 我們走進以變化光線構成的沉浸式裝置。

takeaways.en: Visitors can walk into immersive installations without being allowed to touch every part.
takeaways.zh: 訪客可以走進沉浸式裝置，同時不獲准觸碰每個部分。

brief.meaningEn: Situated or placed in a quiet, hidden or less noticeable position.
brief.meaningZh: 位於或放在安靜、隱蔽或較不顯眼的位置。
brief.grammar: be tucked away behind/beside/in a place; this lesson teaches location, not saved money.
brief.register: Common phrasal verb, often a pleasant description of a small place.
brief.boundaryZh: 不表示完全找不到、非法或沒有人使用；需要交代在哪裏不顯眼。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不顯眼的位置不等於品質低或沒有價值，也不必有人故意秘密隱藏。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述小店或物件的低調位置，區分可找到與直接顯眼。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: The small studio is tucked away behind the market.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 4, table 1, row 5; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: A small reading café is tucked away behind the busy market; a narrow side passage leads to its quiet entrance.
listening.zh: 小閱讀咖啡店隱在繁忙市場後面；一條窄側通道通往安靜入口。

options.en: It occupies the most prominent entrance on the main market frontage.
options.zh: 它佔據市場正面最顯眼入口。

options.en: It is less noticeable behind the market but can be reached through a side passage.
options.zh: 它在市場後面較不顯眼，但可經側通道到達。

options.en: It cannot be reached by any route described.
options.zh: 沒有任何所述路線可到達它。

options.en: It has closed and no longer has an entrance visitors can use.
options.zh: 它已結業，沒有訪客可用入口。

listening.explanationZh: behind 與側通道說明低調但可到達，未表示找不到或結業。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼第一次逛市場的人容易錯過咖啡店？
reply.promptEn: Why might a first-time market visitor miss the café?

options.en: Its entrance is behind the market, off the main route.
options.zh: 入口在市場後面，離開主要路線。

options.en: It is tucked away down a narrow side passage.
options.zh: 它隱在窄側通道內。

options.en: The café is not obvious from the busy front of the market.
options.zh: 從市場繁忙正面不容易看見咖啡店。

options.en: People need to turn off the main path to reach its quiet entrance.
options.zh: 人們要離開主路，轉入安靜入口。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都交代不顯眼位置；金句不是說無法到達。

scene.promptZh: 書店在大樓後院，從街上不顯眼，但沿指示可找到入口。哪句貼切？

options.en: The bookshop is tucked away in the courtyard but can be found by following the signs.
options.zh: 書店隱在後院，但沿告示可找到。

options.en: The bookshop is the prominent display occupying the entire street entrance.
options.zh: 書店是佔據整個臨街入口的顯眼展示。

options.en: The signs lead away from the shop because there is no entrance.
options.zh: 告示把人帶離書店，因為根本沒有入口。

scene.explanationZh: 後院不顯眼與沿指示可達同時成立。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個位置最不像 tucked away？

options.en: A quiet studio behind a row of shops, reached by a side lane.
options.zh: 店舖列後的安靜工作室，經側巷可達。

options.en: A small garden hidden from the main path by a wall.
options.zh: 被牆遮住、主路不易看見的小花園。

options.en: A large stall directly across the main entrance, visible as soon as visitors arrive.
options.zh: 主入口正前的大攤，訪客到達就看見。

contrast.explanationZh: 直接顯眼的位置與較隱蔽、不易注意不同。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「小店 tucked away，就一定沒甚麼值得去」。哪句回應最好？

options.en: Its location tells us it is less obvious, not how good the shop is.
options.zh: 位置告訴我們它較不顯眼，不是店舖品質如何。

options.en: Let us judge the books from how far the entrance is from the street.
options.zh: 只按入口離街多遠判斷書籍吧。

options.en: The hidden position is enough evidence that the service is poor.
options.zh: 隱蔽位置已足以證明服務差。

dialogue.explanationZh: 位置描述不提供品質評價，需看實際商品及服務。

speaking.en: The quiet studio is tucked away behind the row of shops.
speaking.zh: 安靜工作室隱在那列店舖後面。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再交代較不顯眼地方的位置。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你在整理祖母食譜本時，發現一封舊信夾在中間、不容易看見的內頁。你想描述它的位置，不推斷祖母故意保密。用一至兩句英文說明。

examples.en: The old letter was tucked away between the pages of my grandmother’s recipe book, where I found it while tidying.
examples.zh: 舊信隱在祖母食譜本的內頁之間，我整理時找到它。

examples.en: A letter was tucked away inside the recipe book; its location does not tell us why it was put there.
examples.zh: 一封信隱在食譜本裏；它的位置沒有告訴我們為何被放在那裏。

writing.selfCheckZh: 說明物件不顯眼的位置及找到過程，不只因藏在內頁就編造保密動機。

takeaways.en: A little garden is tucked away behind the library.
takeaways.zh: 小花園隱在圖書館後面。

takeaways.en: A shop can be tucked away and still be well worth finding.
takeaways.zh: 店舖可以位置隱蔽，同時仍很值得尋訪。

brief.meaningEn: Become publicly noticed or recognised after being overlooked or little known.
brief.meaningZh: 原本少人知道或被忽略，後來開始公開受到注意或認可。
brief.grammar: step out of the shadows; past stepped; figurative public visibility in this lesson.
brief.register: Conventional light-and-shadow image.
brief.boundaryZh: 不指走到陽光下，也不保證一夜成名、收入提高或再不被忽略；需有之前與之後的可見度轉變。
brief.misconceptionZh: 較晚得到注意不表示之前沒有能力或作品；也不能把一次展示推及所有人的評價。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述被注意的轉變並保留知名度、能力及成果的區別。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Young artists have stepped out of the shadows this year.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 4, table 1, row 6; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: After years of making costumes behind the scenes, the local designers stepped out of the shadows when an exhibition finally credited and displayed their work.
listening.zh: 多年在幕後做服裝後，本地設計師在展覽終於列名並展示作品時，從默默無聞走到人前。

options.en: They stopped producing work because the exhibition hid their names.
options.zh: 他們因展覽隱去姓名而停止創作。

options.en: They began learning basic design only after the exhibition.
options.zh: 他們展覽後才開始學基本設計。

options.en: Their existing work became publicly visible and credited.
options.zh: 他們原有的作品開始公開被看見並獲列名。

options.en: Their pay was confirmed to double immediately after the display.
options.zh: 展示後，他們薪酬已確認立即加倍。

listening.explanationZh: finally credited/displayed 支持從幕後到公開注意，不表示之前不懂或薪酬改變。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼這次展覽對幕後服裝設計師特別重要？
reply.promptEn: Why was the exhibition especially important to the costume designers?

options.en: It gave public credit to work people had often overlooked.
options.zh: 它公開肯定人們常忽略的作品。

options.en: It helped them step out of the shadows.
options.zh: 它幫他們從默默無聞走到人前。

options.en: Visitors could finally see the work with the makers’ names.
options.zh: 訪客終於可連同創作者名字看見作品。

options.en: It brought attention to designers who had long worked quietly behind the scenes.
options.zh: 它讓長期低調幕後工作的設計師受到注意。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都說明可見度與署名的轉變；金句不保證收入或全民知名。

scene.promptZh: 社區攝影師多年有好作品，最近第一次獲公開署名展覽，更多街坊開始認識她。哪句貼切？

options.en: She has stepped out of the shadows as her existing work gains attention.
options.zh: 她原有作品受到注意，已從默默無聞走到人前。

options.en: She had produced no photographs before the exhibition taught her the basics.
options.zh: 她展覽前未拍過照片，展覽才教她基本功。

options.en: The exhibition has removed her name and reduced the work’s visibility.
options.zh: 展覽刪去她名字，降低作品可見度。

scene.explanationZh: 多年已有作品與近期獲注意相容；不是近期才開始有能力。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個結論最不宜由 stepped out of the shadows 得出？

options.en: Previously overlooked work is now more visible.
options.zh: 原被忽略的作品現在較易被看見。

options.en: The person had no skill before receiving publicity.
options.zh: 那人在得到宣傳前沒有技能。

options.en: Public recognition may have increased without proving a change in pay.
options.zh: 公開認可可能增加，而未證明薪酬改變。

contrast.explanationZh: 注意與能力不同，之前默默無聞不等於沒有技能。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「她現在 stepped out of the shadows，之前一定沒有值得看的作品」。哪句澄清最好？

options.en: Let us date her ability from the first press mention rather than look at earlier work.
options.zh: 不看早期作品，只從首次報道日期算她有能力的起點吧。

options.en: The early photographs have no value if they attracted little attention.
options.zh: 早期照片若少人注意，就沒有價值。

options.en: Recognition can arrive later than the work; she may have been creating valuable work for years.
options.zh: 認可可以比作品來得晚；她可能多年來已創作有價值作品。

dialogue.explanationZh: 較晚被注意與較晚才有能力不同，需查看實際早期作品。

speaking.en: The local artists stepped out of the shadows when their work was publicly credited.
speaking.zh: 本地藝術家的作品獲公開署名時，他們從默默無聞走到人前。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再描述幕後工作開始獲公開認可。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：一支地區女子球隊多年認真訓練，最近在聯賽成績進步後，首次獲本地電台訪問，更多人開始認識她們。用一至兩句英文描述公開注意增加，不說她們以前沒有技能。

examples.en: The local team stepped out of the shadows when improved league results led to its first radio interview.
examples.zh: 地區球隊聯賽成績進步後獲首次電台訪問，從默默無聞走到人前。

examples.en: After years of training, the players have stepped out of the shadows as more local people learn about the team through the interview.
examples.zh: 多年訓練後，球員因訪問讓更多街坊認識球隊，已從默默無聞走到人前。

writing.selfCheckZh: 把公開認識與訪問連起來，保留多年已有訓練；不自動加入收入或人人贊同的結論。

takeaways.en: The young craft workers stepped out of the shadows at the public exhibition.
takeaways.zh: 年輕工藝創作者在公開展覽中從默默無聞走到人前。

takeaways.en: An artist can step out of the shadows long after developing strong skills.
takeaways.zh: 藝術家可以在早已練成好技能後，才從默默無聞走到人前。

brief.meaningEn: Towards wider public attention, use or acceptance beyond a smaller specialist group.
brief.meaningZh: 從較小或專門群體走向更廣泛的大眾注意、使用或接受。
brief.grammar: move/come/bring something into the mainstream; mainstream is the widely recognised or established sphere.
brief.register: Common current metaphor used about art, ideas and practices.
brief.boundaryZh: 大眾範圍較廣，不等於人人喜歡、品質必高或作品完全失去特色；需要說明原來與後來的受眾。
brief.misconceptionZh: 進入主流與被所有人認可不同；仍可有小眾來源及不同評價。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述受眾擴大，保留接受程度與品質的證據界限。

listening.en: The documentary moved into the mainstream when national channels began showing it beyond the small local screenings where it started.
listening.zh: 全國頻道開始播放這部紀錄片後，它由原本小型本地放映走進主流。
listening.promptZh: 甚麼變化顯示它走進主流？

options.en: Its audience remained limited to the original small local screenings.
options.zh: 觀眾仍只限原本的小型本地放映。

options.en: It reached a wider public through national broadcasts.
options.zh: 它透過全國廣播接觸更廣泛大眾。

options.en: The channels confirmed that every viewer approved its argument.
options.zh: 頻道確認每位觀眾都贊同它的論點。

options.en: It stopped being shown before any broader audience could see it.
options.zh: 更廣觀眾看見之前，它已停止放映。

listening.explanationZh: 從本地到全國頻道顯示受眾擴大，不代表人人贊同。

reply.promptZh: 這部原本只在本地小型放映的紀錄片後來怎樣了？
reply.promptEn: What happened to the documentary after its small local screenings?

options.en: National channels began showing it to a wider public.
options.zh: 全國頻道開始向更廣大眾播放。

options.en: It moved into the mainstream.
options.zh: 它走進了主流。

options.en: Its audience expanded beyond the local screenings.
options.zh: 觀眾擴大到本地放映以外。

options.en: People outside the original small group could now see it on television.
options.zh: 原本小群體以外的人現在可在電視看到。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描述接觸範圍擴大；金句不保證每人喜歡。

scene.promptZh: 一種原本只在小型社團使用的藝術形式，後來進入多個大眾節目及公開課程。哪句有根據？

options.en: The form has moved into the mainstream as a wider public encounters it.
options.zh: 更多大眾接觸到這種形式，它已走進主流。

options.en: The form remains confined to the original small club with no wider exposure.
options.zh: 這種形式仍只限原本小社團，沒有更廣曝光。

options.en: The wider exposure proves that all critics now rate it equally highly.
options.zh: 更廣曝光證明所有評論者現在都同樣高度評價它。

scene.explanationZh: 大眾節目與公開課程支持受眾擴大，不是所有評論一致。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項推論最不宜由 into the mainstream 得出？

options.en: An idea or work may reach people outside its original specialist group.
options.zh: 想法或作品可接觸原專門群體以外的人。

options.en: Wider attention necessarily means unanimous approval and superior quality.
options.zh: 更廣注意必然表示一致贊同及品質優越。

options.en: A practice can become more widely used while retaining distinctive features.
options.zh: 做法可更廣使用，同時保留特色。

contrast.explanationZh: 範圍擴大不等於一致贊同或品質排名。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「走進主流的作品，就一定失去所有原有特色」。哪句澄清最好？

options.en: Let us infer artistic changes from the larger audience without looking at the work.
options.zh: 不看作品，只從觀眾增加推斷藝術改變吧。

options.en: A wider release means the local dialect has been removed, even without checking the new version.
options.zh: 不用查新版本，更廣發行已表示本地方言被刪去。

options.en: A wider audience does not by itself show that the work’s distinctive features have disappeared.
options.zh: 受眾較廣本身，不顯示作品特色已消失。

dialogue.explanationZh: 受眾及作品特徵是不同判斷，需查看內容變化。

speaking.en: The film moved into the mainstream without losing its local voice.
speaking.zh: 電影走進主流，同時沒有失去本地聲音。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再區分受眾擴大與作品特色。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：修補再用工作坊原本只由一個小型興趣會舉辦，現在圖書館及社區中心也定期提供，吸引原本圈子以外的人。用一至兩句英文描述實踐走向大眾，不保證人人採用。

examples.en: Repair workshops have moved into the mainstream as libraries and community centres offer them to people beyond the original hobby group.
examples.zh: 圖書館及社區中心向原興趣會以外的人提供修補工作坊，它們已走進主流。

examples.en: The repair-and-reuse practice is moving into the mainstream through regular public workshops, although not everyone has adopted it.
examples.zh: 修補再用的做法正透過定期公開工作坊走進主流，雖然不是人人都採用。

writing.selfCheckZh: 用小圈子以外的人及公開服務支持較廣使用，不把主流當作人人採用或品質保證。

takeaways.en: A local style can move into the mainstream through wider distribution.
takeaways.zh: 本地風格可透過更廣發行走進主流。

takeaways.en: Bringing a new idea into the mainstream does not make agreement universal.
takeaways.zh: 把新想法帶進主流，不會令贊同變成普遍一致。
